releases.changelog: An unrecognized harness-pins `schema` and a `grok --version` text without the pinned version warn; the digest-qualified parent and the artifact sha256 still refuse.
`build.sh` reads the canon class's `collab.harness-pins/v2` (collab-resources 1.44.0): the Grok build arguments come from `linux-amd64` and `linux-arm64`. The recipe is unchanged.

**The harness pins come from the canon class.** `CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION`, `CODEX_CLI_VERSION` and `GROK_CLI_VERSION` lose their defaults and, with `GROK_SHA256_AMD64` and `GROK_SHA256_ARM64`, are build arguments whose one declaration is `compatibility/harness-pins.yaml` of `repo-structure/collab-resources` (1.43.0); a build without any of them is refused. Grok is the vendor's versioned binary for the build architecture, verified by its SHA-256, with the vendor's mirror as fallback; the installer script and `GROK_INSTALLER_SHA256` are gone. `build.sh` reads the pins from that file at the checkout's commit and passes them as build arguments; `version.json` drops `harnesses`. A harness bump is a release of the canon class, never of this component. Archify 0.5.0, the bus waiter of subscribe-bus-event 0.1.3, the browser and runtime composition v0.3.82 are unchanged.

Carry the bus waiter of subscribe-bus-event 0.1.3, whose usage error for a repeated match name says the name was given more than once. The block, the installer's record and expected SHA-256, the smoke check and this README move together; nothing else of the image changes.

Carry the bus waiter of subscribe-bus-event 0.1.2. The recipe holds the waiter as its own text in a stage that reads no build context, so every build route installs the same bytes and the waiter never comes from a pack. The build refuses a waiter whose SHA-256 differs from the pin and installs it root-owned under `SUBSCRIBE_BUS_EVENT_ROOT=/opt/subscribe-bus-event` with an installation receipt; the smoke check runs the installed waiter as the session account with no network. Harnesses, Archify 0.5.0, the browser and runtime composition v0.3.82 are unchanged.
Bind verified composition v0.3.82 with Infra 0.3.54 for declared one-person identity and unified menus; retain the published Archify payload.
Build the verified published composition v0.3.80 with Infra 0.3.52 and unchanged Archify 0.5.0; qualify installed components and browser rendering under the agent account.

Bind Archify 0.5.0 and published full runtime v0.3.78, authenticate the complete release build context, and expose the browser to installed Product commands under the agent identity. Consumer registries retain image publication ownership.

Install the shared Archify 0.4.0 release (engine 3.0.1) as released at `7e818e5`, lock `d96e563d…`, payload `0810fb7f…`. **The recipe stops carrying a file count.** A payload digest already fixes the exact set of files, their bytes and their number, so the count beside it verified nothing and had to be retyped in five places on every engine bump; a stale copy of it survived two releases in `smoke.sh`. The Dockerfile, the smoke check and the installation test now answer to the digest alone, and the test derives it with the recipe's own algorithm instead of asserting a number. Adopting this means re-materializing `skills/archify` at its 0.4.0 release commit; a pin at any other tree is refused by the same recipe.

**The image's own toolchain keeps precedence, and the recipes bind the payload Archify actually released.** Two defects found on a managed host while adopting 0.4.1. (1) 0.4.x ended with `ENV PATH=/opt/collab/runtime/bin:${PATH}`, and that directory is the runtime venv's own bin: its `python3`, `pip` and its dependencies' console scripts came before the image's. A session ran Python 3.12 instead of 3.13, and a flavor's ordinary `pip install -r requirements.txt` installed the organization's stack *into* the verified prefix — the pinned publisher boto3 moved under it. The prefix leaves `PATH` entirely; `collab` is reached through its `/usr/local/bin/collab` symlink, which the build now asserts (`command -v collab`) before `collab --version`. Prefix verification is unchanged, and a consumer needs no per-flavor `PATH` repair. (2) 0.4.1 authenticated the digest of the branch tip of `skills/archify`, not of `2232ac49`, the commit that component's 0.3.1 release row publishes — a row is written by the commit after the one it names, so the two trees differ by that row and a consumer pinned at the published commit was refused by the recipe meant to install it. Both recipes now bind payload `d2dc0499…` over the same 82 files and the same lock `c4a0003d…`, and a test holds the bound commit equal to the release row of the pinned version. **Adopting 0.4.2 means re-materializing `skills/archify` at `2232ac49`**; a pin at any other tree is refused. Rehearsed on a managed host from a throwaway consumer re-materialized against this change, with the consumer's per-flavor `PATH` line removed: base, product-manager and tech-lead built, and each answered as uid 1000 with `collab 0.2.5` from `/usr/local/bin/collab`, `python3` 3.13.5 from `/usr/bin`, `pip`/`pip3` from `/usr/bin`, the image stack's boto3 and the publisher's 1.42.36 both intact, `/opt/collab/runtime` holding only the release closure (no boto3, botocore or jinja2) and `collab product diagram deliver lifecycle` passing 9/9 with no warnings. The unpinned tip tree is refused by the same recipe.

Expect the shared Archify 0.3.1 release (`2232ac49`, payload `8beae553…`). 0.4.0 pinned 0.3.0, so a consumer that had already adopted 0.3.1 could not build its base image at all: the recipe refused the payload it carries. Lock digest, engine version, file count and everything else are unchanged.

**The shared Collab runtime is installed in the image.** Archify 0.3.0 and knowledge promotion 4.0.0 execute through the Collab runtime, which no agent image carried: a session had the skills and not the commands they require. The image now installs one exact published release offline from the `collab-release` build context the host prepares (`--build-context`), verified by the release's own installer before installing. Its closure is built for CPython 3.12 exactly, so that interpreter is carried whole in `/opt/collab/python` with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` naming its libraries: `/usr/local` of the agent image, and therefore its own `python3` and Node toolchain, are untouched. `collab` is on `PATH` and symlinked into `/usr/local/bin`. A consumer bumping to 0.4.0 declares its runtime release in the host SRE profile and names the verified artifact directory on the host; a consumer that declares none stays on 0.3.x. Built and probed on a real multi-account host as an agent account without network: `collab 0.2.2`, `repo pack knowledge propose`, `product diagram` and `repo pack transition` answer, and the image's `python3` is unchanged at 3.13.
Install the shared Archify 0.3.0 release (Collab runtime commands) as released at `1720e2af`, payload `ae52d523…`; renderer, browser and publication SDK unchanged.
Authenticate the issue-delivery Archify payload without changing the renderer or browser.

`service-intent-v1` anchors the whole database `url`: user, password and host are `${VAR}` placeholders, so a literal credential or resolved host fails the schema. A schema violation warns on that file; only a credential or resolved address in `url`/`secret` refuses. `archify-publication-v1` takes the producer's `revision`, `index_url` and `workflow_json.presentation`, and a view's explanation may be null or rendered from its specification.

`service-intent-v1`: optional `replaces[]`, the ids of the as-is services a destination document (perspective `to-be` or `implemented`) replaces in a migration; the as-is document declares none, so a reader pairs origin and destination from the destination. The evidence check of `skills/human-artifact-authoring` 0.15.0 reports `replaces` on an as-is document and a document that names itself.

`product-journey-v1` (a design folder's `journey.yaml`: the journeys, their steps with the pages they show and the services they run) and `service-intent-v1` (one document per registered service: observed facts, the data it touches with databases by URN, URL template and secret reference, traced intent and journey bindings). Checked by the evidence check of `skills/human-artifact-authoring` 0.13.0.
Immutable review revisions, navigable indexes and body-visible evidence; publication findings remain advisory.

First release: `qa-journey-v1` (a quality repository's `journey.yaml`: exactly one of `surface.url`, an https address for web channels, or `surface.app`, the `android` and/or `ios` application identifiers for mobile channels; baseline journeys with `epic` and `story` null and a design state on every step; full commits; evidence states and their obligations), `product-mockup-v1` (a design folder's `mockup.yaml`: the design issue, pages by repository path and digest, renders by state, viewport, digest and verified address) and `archify-publication-v1` (the Archify publication manifest). Checked by the evidence check of `skills/human-artifact-authoring` 0.9.0.

**First release** (owner decisions `owner:harness-config-contract-sot`, `owner:harness-config-answers`). Schema `collab.harness-config/v1` and its rule: profiles with `locked` required, `attribute_profiles.agent_developer`, explicit account x agent-type entries with `overrides`; Claude capabilities and models, Codex model and reasoning effort, Grok model. The runtime is the rule's one implementation; what refuses, what warns and what a rejected or removed pin does are part of the rule.
Page and state are not a unique key (every capture is kept by step or file), and the hierarchy's `scale` is authoritative when present.

First release: `journey-captures-v1` (the index a journey run or a lane publishes beside its captures, each named by step, design page and state, with its hierarchy dump and the design folder it belongs to) and `journey-hierarchy-v1` (the element tree of a browser capture: every element carrying the surface's block identifier, with its box and the device scale). Read by the design comparison of the Collab runtime.

First release: the four phases of a sheet bulk load (generate from a versioned template with current values and keep them as the original, submit from the sheet with the person's verified identity token, apply only the changed cells row by row with the screen's commands and permissions, seal the original and the edited copy as read-only records) and `sheet-bulk-load-record-v1`.

"Approvals relayed by the bus", owner-approved wording (owner:auth-wording-gate-2.17.1): the header names the three decisions (OD-054, OD-057, OD-081), and the per-step dispatch of an approved objective keeps the first bullet's conditions (a request from bus.coordinator, its plan digest, meta.dispatch naming the decision and the step); a step runs only after the one before it passed its check and within the enumerated step; another sender, a digest mismatch, a step outside the enumeration, a failed or a divergent step goes back to the owner. Pinned invariants unchanged; the other three bundle files are unchanged from 2.16.0. Pending runtime: composition 0.3.588 bundles it.

New section "Finish line" (OD-081, owner 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-13): a code authorizes a complete objective with a named finish line and its proving check. The objective keeps its segmentation: each step stays its own unit with its own plan, digest, check and receipt, and only the authorization is one; a step whose plan exists only after an earlier step is enumerated as a bounded derivation and its plan is bound to the same authorization. Before the code, a read-only preflight resolves every step the declarations require for the finish line, with preflight blockers as repair steps; person-only steps are listed at the start. Under the code, each step starts when the one before it passed its check, reported as progress; a declared piece the preflight missed is done and recorded in the execution evidence. The owner is asked again only for a step that fails beyond a reversible correction, or diverges (a target outside the enumeration, a materially different effect, or an unnamed root, secret or credential, data-loss or no-way-back effect), for that delta only. "Authorization lifetime" and "Approvals relayed by the bus" name the derivations and the per-step dispatch. Pinned invariants unchanged; the other three bundle files are unchanged from 2.16.0. Pending runtime: the next composition that bundles the gate assets.

"Approvals relayed by the bus" gains a bullet (OD-054 widened, owner 2026-11-10): a candidate's qualification unit inside a development plan the owner authorized is approved the same way, and when the operator already showed its code for a unit inside such an approved objective, the exact code that the canon's `bus.coordinator` sends back as a `reply` is the exact echo, recorded by its sequence; any other sender or a unit outside the objective is not an echo. The other three bundle files are unchanged from 2.15.0.

New section "Approvals relayed by the bus": inside a round whose plan the owner approved, a unit named in a dispatch from the canon's `bus.coordinator` (plan artifact matching its digest, `meta.dispatch` naming the owner's decision id and the unit) runs with no echo, recorded under the dispatch seq, digest and decision id; anything outside still needs the exact echo (OD-054). The code the person a notice went to types in the operator bus's code form, relayed by `bus.operator_bus`, is that person's exact echo (OD-057). Pinned invariants unchanged; canonical digest `4c076f72`. Pending runtime: composition 0.3.572 bundles it.

`check_instructions.py` reports each finding with a code as `ERROR` or `WARNING` and exits 0 on retired version spellings, request position and private gate copies; only an operator-authored code, a code shown before the unit and an altered shared gate fail (#632). The README states that a gate release without a matching readiness record is a release-integrity warning.

The numbered mutation contract names the lifecycle transition helper of the repository-work-selection skill as the path for a `lifecycle:` label change: one write that replaces the label set, previewed with `--dry-run`, applied with the previewed labels as precondition and its response as readback; every other repository delivery change keeps the typed route. Mechanism, `confirm-gate.md` and schemas unchanged.

A precondition's baseline is the content the API returned, never a shell redirection (enviaflores/collab-resources#139); content is compared before declaring drift, and a false positive is corrected by a replacement plan under the existing authorization. A later operation of the same plan validates against the state its earlier verified operations left on that target or its parent (enviaflores/collab-resources#334); a change nobody in the plan made is still drift.

The numbered mutation contract keeps every authority rule and leaves the mechanics the installed runtime performs and states to the runtime (`collab repo delivery-mutation describe`) and the base's delivery CLI reference: 5.5 KB of always-loaded text instead of 8.2 KB. Schemas and confirm-gate.md unchanged.
Declare finite typed lifecycle writers for issue changes, exact comments and exact-head merge under the existing objective authorization.
Compact objective authorization without increasing inherited instruction debt; preserve scope, echo, plan binding and merge safeguards.
One authorization per operator-defined objective; eliminate repeated pending requests, audit fragmentation, and preserve scope across phases and recovery.
Publish the complete version-two mutation contract and schemas with explicit runtime compatibility.

Present the unit first and end every approval message, and every later message while a code is pending, with the request to type the exact bold code; reject instructions that move that request off the final line.
Preserve authorization for equivalent execution adjustments, including merge methods for the same PR and head; link replacement plans without renewing the code.
Inherit one shared harness gate and mutation bundle; reject persona copies while preserving objective-scoped authorization and declared ungated headless execution.
Gate external effects and concrete local risks; preserve authorization through reversible local iteration until verified objective completion.

**Artifact repository contract.** Class-pinned `schema/artifact-repository-v1.schema.json` (`artifact-repository-v1`) for the canon's `governance/artifact-repositories.yaml`: the organization's artifact repositories, the default one, `ephemeral_retention_days` (fewer than 30 warns and 30 applies) and per repository its driver, flavor, bucket, endpoint, public base URL, private prefix, signed-link ceiling and credential binding reference, never a value (owner decisions D3 and D7, 2026-11-16; rule in `skills/artifact-publication`). Schema set 1.14.

**A migration keeps the legitimate AS-IS conduct** (owner decision, 2026-11-16). The canon scaffold's migration defaults and migration epic template drop the integrity or security correction as conformance: conduct stays the AS-IS, only integrity or security corrections that preserve it enter (with defect, change and evidence), every other defect goes to the follow-up epic under the initiative, and nothing departs from the AS-IS conduct.

**A platform may own permissions** (owner decision `owner:platform-can-own-permissions`, option A): a `PERM-###` declares exactly one owner, `Business-Unit:` or `Platform:`; the key is `<owner-slug>/<domain-slug>/<resource-slug>/<action>`, the owner participates in the domain, and the authority repository has the same owner (one owner per repository, owner decision). A merge on the canonical repository is the explicit approval of a permission. The authorization catalog moves to schema `1.5`: a `platforms` array, the `platforms` of each domain, and exactly one of `business_unit` or `platform` on each permission; the seeded schema, the governance text and the registry READMEs follow. A reader accepts `1.4` and `1.5` (`1.5` adds `platforms[]`, `domains[].platforms` and `permissions[].platform`; a permission may carry `platform` and no `business_unit`); an unknown version number is warned, not refused. The render refuses to publish a permission with two owners, none, or an authority repository of another owner, naming the record; the validator and the record creators only warn, and a repeated owner or authority key with different values counts as two owners. Any other repeated metadata key warns in every family. Set `AUTHORIZATION_CATALOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` to `1.5` by hand at adoption; the render warns when it is below `1.5`. Adopt with collab-resources-sre 0.52.0.

**UX/UI reach is the organization** (owner decision, 2026-11-13). The operational stewardship document states that the `UX-UI-Of` role is the person's responsibility, not a limit on the agent's reach, which is any visual surface of the organization bounded only by what its person's GitHub login can do. Embeds EDR-001 with its dated amendment (ecosystem-decisions 0.44.0). The 1.76.0 notes paraphrase in English the owner quotation they cited. Existing canons adopt the class files.

**`UX-UI-Of` accepts platforms** (owner, 2026-11-13: "B: cambiar la regla para incluir plataformas"): the role names `BU-###` or `PLAT-###`, like `Product-Manager-Of`. The canon-record schema and the published stewardship schema type `ux_ui_of` with the shared business-unit-or-platform definition (the unused `business_unit_only_roles` definition is removed); the stewards guide, the operational stewardship document and the canon `AGENTS.md` relation list state the widened rule. No coverage warning for either. Existing canons port the schema change into their seeded `schemas/stewardship-v1.schema.json`; no record changes.

**The organization web console declaration** (owner, 2026-11-13): `schema/web-console-v1.schema.json` (`collab.web-console/v1`) and the seeded-once `governance/web-console.yaml` (`web_console: null`). An explicit declaration names only the console's public https base URL; runtimes build their links from it (the operator bus acknowledgement links to `/users/me/requests/<chat id>`). Existing canons adopt the schema and seed only the missing file.

an executor checks execution only and changes a step only for an unsupported typed operation or a state without rollback the plan does not name, replying once with a `defect`. `skills/host/_contracts/merge-authorization.md`: the coordinator prepares every plan itself on its own host with `collab infra merge-plan prepare --pack <checkout at P> --pull-request <n>... --output-dir <dir> [--fetch] [--developer <id>] [--central-host ... --central-operator <id>] --ttl-hours <request_ttl_hours> --emit` (Infra 0.3.412, cli 0.3.80), whose `--emit` uploads `merge-plan-<plan_id>.json` as the plan's bus artifact (rules 5, 6, 11, 25), `expires_at = created_at + ttl_hours` (rule 13), asks the owner directly (rule 12), dispatches by row type (rule 17); executors keep `merge-plan check --plan <plan> --host <provider>/<host-id>` and run as written (rules 18, 27); no operator plans, with no transition from the central host; rule 21, every seed, cloud ones included, is the consuming host's services operator's, through the typed `seed` of its root services broker; rule 29, a missing typed operation is built by that host's host operator as an extension in the organization's pack (`extensions/collab/`), through the pull requests the operators' GitHub App already opens, the owner authorizing each merge, a source-of-truth change by the developer, the coordinator routing it once; one closing format; rule 30, the service source is a platform row. `skills/host/_contracts/secret-distribution.md`: "Layered limits" (guard `infra-secret-limits-layered-v1`), stated once: the central broker's per-host grants, the host role's IAM policy, the host's root services broker and its typed operations (its `seed` writes only declared entries the central grant covers, create-only), the secrets console's per-user permissions; Enforcement names the host's onboarding identity, used by its services broker for the typed `seed`, as the declared path. `typed-operation.md`: the broker's host-level `seed`. `contracts/infrastructure-merge-plan.schema.json`: every unit requires `row` (`platform`, `service`), and `operator` can name the developer. The central operator operates the central infrastructure, its cloud access and the central host and neither plans nor coordinates nor seeds; the host operator installs its host's SREs and builds its typed operations as pack extensions; the services operator seeds through its broker and answers a read-only question outside its assignments with the missing typed operation. The three operator personas: operating tempo rules 2 and 9, no restatement of the shared bus rules or bus economy, drift outside a dispatched row is a follow-up, one report format; the defect cycle and the service change cycle follow. Released after #766 (1.56.0, guard `parameters-never-recreate-v1`), whose rule and test are kept; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow.

**Parameters and secrets never recreate a container.** `skills/host/_contracts/service-change-cycle.md` rule 10 (guard `parameters-never-recreate-v1`): a container, session, runner or virtual machine is recreated, and an image rebuilt, only for its toolchain (image, harness pins, declared structure); a parameter or a secret reaches the running process through a mounted file it re-reads (mounted through its directory or rewritten through its own inode) or a typed reload the plan enumerates as `reload` and the bound canary checks; a plan never counts content that moves only with a parameter or a secret as a reason to recreate, nor folds an earlier parameter drift into a recreate another change causes; a service that can do neither is named unreloaded and its gap is a defect of that service. `_contracts/typed-operation.md` states the split for `plan`; the central, host and services operator personas cite rule 10; `tests/test_parameters_never_recreate_contract.py` guards the citations and the export; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow.

**One coordinator, the rollout coordinator; the owner decides every rollout.** `skills/host/_contracts/merge-authorization.md`: rules 1-3, every merged pull request, whoever merged it, reaches only the canon's `bus.coordinator` as the event bus's system notice, which is its rollout request; a `Collab-Merged-By: <developer>` trailer is context (the owner authorized that development), never a silence signal, and the developer sends at most a `status` or an `ack`; rules 4 and 5, no operator analyzes a merge and the central operator plans only on the coordinator's request; rule 15, the owner decides every merge plan, asked each time through the coordinator's question tool, with no standing delegation, and the central operator never asks the owner; rule 17, the coordinator alone dispatches every row (service rows to their operators, the central host's to the central operator, platform rows to the developer); rules 18-20, 24 and 27, rows report and close with the coordinator. Rule 29: one coordinator, the rollout coordinator, which serializes hosts and writers; the request lifecycle (development to the developer, which asks the owner, develops and merges); typed-capability gaps (the host operator develops and smoke-tests on its host in the strict order disposable instance, host with verified rollback, owner approval, opens the issue and pull request and hands them to the developer through the coordinator, never merging or rolling out); the developer and the break-glass are not coordinators, and the break-glass acts on a host only inside an incident it declares. Rule 30: platform rows run by the developer on the coordinator's dispatch. `_contracts/agent-bus.md` (defects of typed operations), the service change cycle, the central, host and services operator personas and `contracts/agent-bus.schema.json` follow; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow.

**The development coordinator; the break-glass is for break-glass only.** `skills/host/_contracts/merge-authorization.md` rules 12, 15, 29 and 30: up to three request-based coordinators, the canon's `development_coordinator` (`sre/collab-developer`), `autonomous_coordinator` and `bus.coordinator`; a request no coordinator started goes to the development coordinator, then the autonomous one, then the bus coordinator; when two act on one decision the development coordinator's prevails. The development coordinator leads development and rollouts (takes plans, sets order and priority, holds or drops rows, hands numbered plans) and runs the platform rows of approved plans by script through the organization's coordinator access route, with a backup per host (rule 30); a canon without one leaves each platform row to its host operator. No row is dispatched to the break-glass and nothing waits for it; it prevails only on the hosts of an incident it declares ("BGS declares incident <id>: <hosts>") until it closes it, and may take a row only there. The central, host and services operator personas and `_contracts/agent-bus.md` follow; declarative-v1.json copies follow.

**The services operator names its typed client.** `skills/host/services-operator/SKILL.md` no longer tells the persona to use `operator-resource`, the pre-0.3 client no current runtime installs: the persona uses `/usr/local/libexec/collab-runtime-python -I -m collab.cli infra service <operation> --service <assignment-id>`, which reaches the root-owned services broker; its lifecycle operations are `status`, `doctor`, `plan`, `apply`, `canary` and `rollback`, and `reconcile`, `maintenance`, `prepare-host` and `publish-state` serve the units that name them. The agent prompt, the README (the broker re-resolves the installed services authority) and the adapter contract's public routes follow; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. Text only; no behavior change.

**Each coordinator coordinates the requests that reach it.** `skills/host/_contracts/merge-authorization.md` rule 29 no longer follows the owner's presence: the canon names two coordinators (`bus.coordinator`, the owner's break-glass session, and the `autonomous_coordinator`), both may message every identity directly; the central operator sends the request and the closure to the coordinator that started the objective or thread the merge belongs to, and to the autonomous coordinator when none did; either coordinator's reply is the decision with no ratification, and the bus coordinator's prevails when both act. The break-glass is the owner's break-glass SRE, leads the whole infrastructure and lives only while the owner is behind it (never autonomous, unattended or in a loop; acting without the owner is a warning). When its work asks for priority over a request queued with or by the autonomous coordinator, that request is paused or reordered and the break-glass's goes first; a pause is not a cancellation. Rules 12, 15 and 20, the central operator persona and `skills/host/_contracts/agent-bus.md` follow; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow.

**Platform rows run by the break-glass, without a second gate.** `skills/host/_contracts/merge-authorization.md` rule 30: a platform row (runtime prefix, pack checkout, authority, service-runtime metadata, operator workspaces, state publication) of an approved plan is applied by the owner's break-glass by script on every host at once, under the plan's approval alone; no operator presents, re-checks or echoes it; the central operator dispatches platform rows to the break-glass identity, never to the host operators; operators keep their code for service applies, destructive or billable units, seeds and grants; one plan an hour at most, or one when the owner asks. The three personas and `sre/breaking-glass-sre` follow; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. Owner decision of 2026-11-03 (#725).

**The reveal policy and the retirement plan pinned from the canon.** The pack carries `contracts/secret-reveal.schema.json` and `contracts/secret-retirements.schema.json` (the collab-resources 1.38.0 schemas under this class's identifiers). `contracts/secret-vaults-pin.schema.json`: the vault catalog and its assignments stay first and required; after them the pin lists any of the optional canon declarations, each once, in this order: entry sources, host domains, service bindings, reveal policy, retirement plan (2 to 7 files), so a pack may pin the reveal policy before its bindings. `skills/host/_contracts/secret-vaults.md` follows; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. Pairs with Infra 0.3.380.

**The coordinator follows the owner's presence.** `skills/host/_contracts/merge-authorization.md` rule 29: the session the canon names as `bus.coordinator` is the coordinator only while the owner is connected in it (the hub shows the identity online, or an owner message from it is in progress); at every other time (autonomous mode) the coordinator is the canon's `autonomous_coordinator` (collab-resources 1.40.0). The central operator sends the request and the closure to the coordinator in role and accepts the autonomous coordinator's reply as the coordinator's delegated decision, with no ratification; when both act on one decision, the bus coordinator's prevails. A presence it cannot read counts as autonomous mode, with a warning; a canon without `autonomous_coordinator` keeps the bus coordinator alone. Rules 12 and 15 and the central operator persona follow; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow.

**Configuration keys and no blobs.** The pack's `contracts/secret-vault-assignments.schema.json` copy follows collab-resources 1.39.0: `class: config` entries with `key` and `value`, and no entry is a file blob, so a canon with configuration keys pins through `collab infra canon inspect`. Collab Infra 0.3.376 never seeds a config entry, never requires it in the vault-dependency preflight, and delivers its declared value from the pinned canon.

**Secret declarations pinned from the canon.** The pack carries `contracts/secret-vault-sources.schema.json`, `contracts/secret-host-domains.schema.json` and `contracts/secret-bindings.schema.json` (the collab-resources 1.36.0 schemas under this class's identifiers). `contracts/secret-vaults-pin.schema.json`: the pin lists 2 to 5 files, the vault catalog and assignments first, then the sources, the host domains and the bindings, all from one canon commit. `host-declaration.schema.json` `domains` and `host-service-assignment.schema.json` `secret_bindings` (no longer required) apply only in a pack that pins no canon copy; the Infra runtime reads only the pinned copy and pack validation refuses the field beside it. `skills/host/_contracts/secret-vaults.md`: where the declarations live, one source, and no vault entry holds a blob (a legacy blob is only a per-key source; a rendered file is assembled at delivery). `secret-distribution.md` and the host-operator skill follow; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow.

**Coordinator and break-glass.** `skills/host/_contracts/merge-authorization.md` rule 29: the owner holds two roles on the bus and one session may hold both; the act, not the identity, tells them apart. The coordinator decides with one `reply` (partial approval kept; `destructive` and `billable_cloud` by name) and runs no unit. The break-glass, operated by the owner, executes a row when the owner orders it or the row's operator cannot act, announces "BGS takes row N", and its report (plan, row, host, result, units, evidence, state commit, final P and runtime, canary, rollback) closes the row as the operator's would. It leads the orchestration whenever it enters: it may take over a plan, set priorities, hold or drop a row and hand any operator a numbered plan; the central operator records and follows. Every approved row is dispatched at once; a host waits only on a declared dependency, one writer per host; a superseding plan keeps closed rows. The central operator persona and `sre/breaking-glass-sre` follow; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. Agreed on the bus with the central operator (#725).

**The coordinator's reply is the decision, identifier mismatches warn, and operators hold nothing for each other.** `skills/host/_contracts/merge-authorization.md`: rule 12, the request is at most 2,000 characters with the plan as the artifact and a refused message is shortened and resent the same way; rule 15, the coordinator is the owner's own harness identity, its reply is the decision and nobody ratifies it; rule 17, a dispatch carries the row, never the runtime; rule 18, only `required_version_unmet` holds a unit, every other mismatch (digest, pin, runtime identity, persona closure, host check) is a warning in the evidence; rule 20, one closure of at most 2,000 characters; new section Between operators (guard `infra-merge-between-operators-v1`), rule 28: no hold and no evidence requests between operators, one message per decision or result, never a reply to a reply, and the owner's own session may run any row directly. The three personas carry the same bus economy; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. Evidence: #725. Pairs with Infra 0.3.370 (the hub client pin and the runtime identity warn).

**Merge planning fails open, and a required version refuses.** `skills/host/_contracts/merge-authorization.md` rules 21-24: the dependencies report is advisory input. When it cannot run, the plan records a warning in `warnings` and proceeds. `vault_entries` and `catch_up` are best-effort, and activation and seed still come before the consumer when known. `vault_not_ready` stays the one vault gate. New guard `infra-merge-planning-code-v1`: rule 25, plan with the composition P pins (`install.py run` from delivered, verified releases; `planned_with`); rule 26, `requires_version` only for a unit whose data safety or recovery path depends on a fix, citing it; rule 27, `collab infra merge-plan check` refuses `required_version_unmet` against the tool, P's composition or, with `--host`, the host's installed runtime. The schema gains `planned_with`, `warnings` and `requires_version`. The personas follow. Requires Infra 0.3.364.

**The journey flows service template replaces the mobile flows one.** `service-templates/ai/journey-flows-mcp` is renamed from `mobile-flows-mcp` in one change, with no alias. It has SRE `journey-flows-mcp-sre` 0.2.0, capability `infra.journey-flows-mcp.v2` and lock schema `collab.journey-flows-mcp.lock/v1`. Both surfaces, `/mobile` and `/web`, are served, and `caller-accounts` becomes an optional, legacy input. The runtime contract states the installation of `runners/journey-flows-mcp` 0.3.1 or later: the app export, `app.py` and `weed` run directly, `gitconfig`, `JOURNEY_FLOWS_*` names, the per-repository delivery layout and preinstalled Playwright browsers. The declarative export, `manifest.yaml`, the catalog and `service_templates` own `services/ai/journey-flows-mcp/*` and no longer expect `services/ai/mobile-flows-mcp/*`.

**A service never lands before the vault entries it needs.** `skills/host/_contracts/merge-authorization.md` (guard `infra-merge-vault-dependencies-v1`): an assignment's `secret_bindings` are the vault entries it requires (an entry inside a declared vault's location, or on a broker-delivery host the host's copy of a declared domain entry); pack validation refuses one the canon does not declare or assign to that host and service; `collab infra service plan` refuses `vault_not_ready` (`not_declared`, `inactive`, `not_assigned`, `not_seeded`) before any member. Rule 21: a row whose entries are not ready gets the vault activation and the seed before it in the same plan, the seed flagged `billable_cloud` and approved by name, and the row waits on its `vault_entries`; rule 22: a consumer of a ready vault that is not adopted is a mandatory `catch_up` row of the next plan; rule 23: the daily `collab infra vaults dependencies report`, published to `infra-services-operation`; rule 24: no workaround. `contracts/infrastructure-merge-plan.schema.json`: a unit may carry `vault_entries` and `catch_up`. The central and services operator personas follow; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. Requires Infra 0.3.360 and secrets broker 0.7.2.

**Every unit closes with its state publication.** `skills/host/_contracts/state-plane.md` (guard `state-publication-closes-every-unit-v1`): publishing state is the closing step of every unit that changes what a host or a service reports, and no unit closes without it. Every typed host operation that changes what the host reports (authority, runtime or runtime adoption, services runtime, operator workspaces, access keys) ends by publishing the host inventory, whoever runs it; a change made outside a typed operation closes with `collab infra host inventory --reconcile`; a unit that changed a service without a terminal `apply` or `rollback` closes with `collab infra service publish-state`. A failed publication never refuses and never rolls back: it is recorded as pending and retried by the host's state timer, or by the service's next transition or `publish-state`. A unit closes with the state commit, or `degraded` naming the pending publication. The host and services operator personas carry the rule in their workflow and unit closure; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. Requires Infra 0.3.340.

**A secret binding row may name its variable.** `contracts/host-service-assignment.schema.json`: both `secret_bindings` row kinds (AWS and Infisical) accept an optional `variable` (`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,127}$`), the environment variable the bound entry is delivered as; the entry's name need not match it. Rows without it validate as before, so no `schema_version` change; the `declarative-v1.json` embedded copy follows. The Infra runtime reads it from its next release, where a malformed value only warns and is left out.

**A vault may live at a grouped namespace location.** `scripts/secret_vaults_contract.py` `namespace_of` accepts `<namespace>/<group>/.../<vault>/` (one to six groups, `MAX_GROUPS = 6`) beside `<namespace>/<vault>/`, so `key_ref`, the validator's namespace warning and the binding boundary follow; `skills/host/_contracts/secret-vaults.md` (guard `infra-secret-vaults-namespaces-v1`) states the rule; `contracts/secret-vaults.schema.json` (the canon class 1.35.0 schema, byte for byte) and `contracts/host-declaration.schema.json` descriptions follow; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. The Infra runtime carries the script byte for byte from its next release.

**A merge reaches the central operator alone, which plans from observed state and asks before any update.** New shared contract `skills/host/_contracts/merge-authorization.md` (guard `infra-merge-authorization-v1`): the event bus sends each merge of the pack's repository as a direct system `request` to the central operator only, never on `infra-services-operation`; one plan per merge or batch from each host's published observed state on `state` (installed pack commit, runtime, authority, services): per host from → to, the units its host and services operators run, the expected restarts (normally none) and the order, never a unit that deletes, revokes or narrows a secret, credential or grant; one `attention` request with the plan artifact and digest to the canon's bus coordinator, decidable for the canon's `request_ttl_hours` (collab-resources 1.34.0; 12 h, 1 to 168); dispatch only after an approval that names the digest; each operator applies its row with its usual gate code. New `contracts/infrastructure-merge-plan.schema.json` (`collab.infrastructure-merge-plan/v1`, exported under `infrastructure/contracts/`). The three operator personas carry the guard.

**The agents hub renders a host's terminal route and known_hosts line from its registry.** `contracts/host-declaration.schema.json`: optional `ssh_host_keys` (`type` ed25519/ecdsa/rsa, `fingerprint` `SHA256:...`). `service-templates/platform/agents-hub` (0.1.3 candidate): `host_registry` may declare `edge` (`file`, `service`, `config_path`, `path_prefix`) and `known_hosts`; the registry's terminal hosts are rendered into a marked region of the edge file, written in place (a single-file bind mount) and loaded with `caddy reload`, with no recreate. Each terminal host with declared `ssh_host_keys` gets a known_hosts line read with ssh-keyscan and accepted only on a fingerprint match. Existing routes and lines are kept. `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. Requires Infra 0.3.320.

**A unit closes without host hygiene; hygiene is its own authorized unit.** `skills/host/_contracts/unit-workspace.md`: a unit ends with `unit-workspace close --apply`, never with `--hygiene`; `collab infra host hygiene --apply` deletes what a live host may still need (build caches, images, runtimes), so it runs only as its own unit the person authorizes with a code, after its dry-run report, never at a close, on the daily harness refresh or because the disk budget warns; a disk-budget warning is reported `degraded` and never acted on by itself. The `host-operator` and `central-operator` personas, `service-change-cycle.md` rule 9 and `operator-harnesses.md` (the daily refresh only reports the hygiene dry-run) follow; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. No runtime change.

**A vault catalog declares its environment namespaces.** `contracts/secret-vaults.schema.json` (the canon class 1.33.0 schema, byte for byte): optional `namespaces`, each a name or `{name, key_ref}`. `skills/host/_contracts/secret-vaults.md` (guard `infra-secret-vaults-namespaces-v1`): a new vault lives at `<namespace>/<vault>/`; any other prefix stays valid and warns; the typed path writes no registrar name outside the declared namespaces; a write into `<namespace>/<vault>/` uses the namespace's `key_ref` when it names one; a host's binding boundary admits each listed domain at `<namespace>/<domain>/` beside the earlier locations; the console shows the namespace. `scripts/secret_vaults_contract.py`: `namespaces`, `namespace_of`, `key_ref`, `writable` and the warnings. `contracts/host-declaration.schema.json` `domains` description follows; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. The Infra runtime enforces the rule from its next release; an earlier runtime reads the list and ignores it.

**A host access policy declares the authorized keys each account holds exactly.** `contracts/host-access-policy.schema.json`: both policy versions take an optional `authorized_keys` (`$defs/authorized_keys`): `accounts` and `/etc/ssh` key `files`, each a list of key ids into the pack's key catalog `infrastructure/hosted/keys/catalog.json` (classes `break-glass`, `coordinator`, `hub-terminal`, `person`, `retired`), plus `sshd.settings` (`PermitRootLogin prohibit-password`, `PasswordAuthentication no`, `KbdInteractiveAuthentication no`, `PubkeyAuthentication yes`) and `sshd.retired_drop_ins`. `skills/host/_contracts/host-registration.md`: the host operator applies it with `collab infra host authorized-keys reconcile` (backup first, removed keys recorded by fingerprint; `check` warns on drift); a root declaration keeps a break-glass and a coordinator key; a person key goes only in that person's own account. `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. Requires Infra 0.3.304.

**The two-factor digest confirmation joins with the phase V4 step-up.** `skills/host/services-operator/SKILL.md` and `skills/host/_contracts/secret-vaults.md` say what the secrets-broker SRE 0.4.0 already says: until the identity provider step-up ships (phase V4), the gate code typed in the operator's session authorizes a typed vault change; from V4 the person's two-factor confirmation of the plan digest is also required. `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. No runtime change.

**No grant reconciliation removes or narrows a grant.** `skills/host/_contracts/secret-vaults.md`: `cloud reconcile-github-app-access` and `cloud reconcile-vault-access` keep the owned statements when nothing is derived (a host cut to broker delivery, a vault no longer carried, an App source no longer declared) and widen a narrower derived grant with the secrets granted today; a broker-delivery host gets no new grant; retiring a grant is a separate owner decision. `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. Requires Infra 0.3.298.

**Hosts declare secret domains; a domain vault holds each shared entry once.** `contracts/host-declaration.schema.json`: optional `domains`, each a vault the canon declares at `<vault root>/<domain>/`; a host may belong to several. `skills/host/_contracts/secret-vaults.md` (guard `infra-secret-vaults-domains-v1`): membership admits the domain's location in the host's secret binding boundary (a provider's name admits nothing) while assignments still decide what it receives; `cloud seed-domain-vault-entries` creates the canon's declared entries from the per-host copies inside the registrar's process, only while every copy holds the same value, never overwriting an entry or touching a copy; `cloud reconcile-service-secret-access` never removes a grant and grants no domain entry per host; a registration may declare no bootstrap secret and central onboarding derives the bootstrap identity. `scripts/secret_vaults_contract.py`: an assignment naming a host the pack does not declare warns and carries nothing. `host-registration.md` and `central-runtime.md` follow; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. Requires Infra 0.3.292.

**The agents-hub presence canary reads live presence.** `agents-hub-sre` 0.1.2: online while the client holds its presence channel on the websocket server (its channel list, read through the app's `presence.app_service`), else a last authenticated call under 180 s old made after the last live leave; a last-seen refresh alone no longer counts. Requires Infra 0.3.276.

**agents-hub-sre requires Infra 0.3.270.** `agents-hub-sre` 0.1.1: the runtime that registers the `agents-hub` provider is Infra 0.3.270 (composition 0.3.392); the 1.33.0 row and the 0.1.0 changelog named 0.3.268.

**The agents-hub service template and the operator safety rules.** New `service-templates/platform/agents-hub` (`agents-hub-sre` 0.1.0, catalog `runtime_provider` `agents-hub`, capability `infra.agents-hub.v2`): the agents management package's host application as one Docker Compose project, adopted in place; a dependency-aware plan that names the services a change recreates and restarts the declared dependents of a recreated data store; the data store's own env file; a canary after every apply (health 200, every admitted hub identity refreshing its last-seen within the window, a websocket held past it) that rolls back to the previous image and env; the bubble's hosts and terminals rendered from the pack's host declarations. New shared contract `skills/host/_contracts/operator-safety.md` (guard `infra-operator-safety-v1`), linked from the three operator personas. Requires Infra 0.3.268.

**Declarative services and pinned organization extensions.** `contracts/service-operation.schema.json` and its exported copy accept `schema_version` 3: `engine` (`docker-compose`, `systemd`, `launchd`, `pinned-binary`, `python-service`; per-role data and SHA-256-pinned artifacts) and `operations` (install, upgrade, status, doctor, canary, rollback, retire as data); new check kinds `unit-active`, `job-running`, `container-running`, `file-present` with value references; a version-3 contract takes no `command` check. `CONTRACT.md`, the scaffold `AGENTS.md` (rule 6) and `docs/service-contract.md` name the declarative form and the pinned organization extension (`extensions/collab/`, `compatibility/collab-extensions.lock.json`, capability `infra.extensions.v1`). Additive: no template moves. `declarative-v1.json` carries the changed files. Requires Infra 0.3.260 and cli 0.3.70.

**The headscale surface's TLS termination is the bound front kind.** `headscale-sre` 0.1.1: the public surface's `tls_termination` is the bound `front-kind` (`nginx`), as the host service assignment schema defines it (`nginx` \| `service`), not the off-schema `front`. `declarative-v1.json` carries the changed files. Requires Infra 0.3.256.

**The headscale service template: an overlay-network coordination server and its front, adopted in place.** New `service-templates/platform/headscale` (`service_template: headscale`, SRE `headscale-sre` 0.1.0): two systemd roles (`control`, `front`); the server configuration and the front site declared verbatim, a service document with the protected nodes, public DNS, backup retention and the policy's authority (`management-api` for a database policy, `pack` for a file policy); a configuration with a secret value refuses. The lock (`collab.headscale.lock/v1`) pins the installed executable and its packaged unit (adoption) or a staged artifact (upgrade). Adoption records the loaded revision without a restart; changes restart only in apply, after a database backup read as the server's own account; the canary requires the protected nodes online before the change to reconnect, other nodes and public DNS warn, and a failing canary rolls back; `retired` stops the server and keeps its data. The template joins the declarative export (`infra.headscale.v2`). Requires Infra 0.3.254.

The App vault is assigned to `host-operator`, `central-operator` and `services-operator` (GitHub access section of the three personas). `skills/host/_contracts/service-api.md`: release to hosts. secrets-broker SRE 0.4.0. **Operating tempo; the operators keep to the unit's objective.** The central, host and services operator personas open, right after their identity, with one identical `Operating tempo` section (guard `operator-operating-tempo-v1`) that sets the pace and grants no authority: objective first (what done means, its target and evidence; stop when it exists), an explicit numbered plan executed in order, one code early (the whole unit with its code in the first reply; a code typed in the session's terminal is the human's echo whoever types it; a code that arrives while none is pending is answered at once with the unit and the model's own code), verify once (only the mutation contract's readback around each write repeats; typed commands instead of ad hoc scripts), no acknowledgements, warn and continue (only integrity, security or real authority stops, rule 8; a blocker is reported at once), the canary is the test, and one final report. The personas no longer copy the `multi-account-host-sre` development and synchronization doctrine (guard `sre-developer-pr-materializes-state-v3`); a short pointer states it belongs to that role and that their own fixes follow the lean defect cycle. `sre/agent-bus.md` rule 7: answer only what asks for an answer; `operator-harnesses.md` and the services operator's first message follow it. `declarative-v1.json` carries the changed files.

**No host is onboarded without services; host service templates.** `host-onboarding-sre` 0.2.0: every onboarding installs both operators of the new host, its host operator and its services operator, each admitted on the hub, and the declaration assigns at least one enabled service to that services operator; a host that would run no service is registered capacity, never an onboarding. Eight phases: declaration, central enrollment, host bootstrap, **operators** (the host operator by root, then the services operator by the new host operator under the person's code), **console and bubble** (each operator's identity in the host's bubble with a web terminal attached to its own session), verification, publication and closure. The closure is a checklist: host identity, both operators admitted, terminals, the host publisher's first state, the delivery consumed and revoked or expired, the central name resolved over the overlay network, and no prompt residue; an item that does not hold keeps the onboarding open. New templates in the declarative export, both on launchd: `service-templates/ai/local-model-serving` (`local-model-serving-sre` 0.1.0, `infra.local-model-serving.v2`; the lock pins the installed executable or a staged artifact; declared conflicting jobs and other instances are stopped) and `service-templates/ai/mobile-flows-mcp` (`mobile-flows-mcp-sre` 0.1.0, `infra.mobile-flows-mcp.v2`; the lock pins each role's installed program and trees; a hand-started server on a declared port is stopped; secrets as the account's read-only files). `contracts/service-operation.schema.json`: the role orchestrator gains `launchd` (additive). `docs/hub-host-registry.md`: design-only proposal to derive the hub's host registry from pack declarations. Hardening from the first run (`host-onboarding-sre` 0.2.0): a delivery is refused once expired, completed or revoked, except the same enrollment's own callback within its grace; a successful enrollment revokes its delivery; the canary is `pending` before the prompt runs and judges identity apart from the closed delivery; plan warns when the enrollment name does not resolve over the overlay network; the prompt removes its own copies; publishing state is the normal last step of `service-change-cycle.md`; `references/prompt-delivery.md` is a design note for console delivery. `skills/host/services-operator`: an external assignment is operated only when its provider source is installed and its SRE names the services operator (`github-runners-host-sre` 0.21.0 does: the services operator runs the runner service, the native macOS executor's included; host preparation, native operator maintenance, logbook and telemetry stay with the host operator; the `<harness>-ghro` launcher retires).

**Every unit prepares and closes its workspace; hygiene is part of the closure.** New shared contract `skills/host/_contracts/unit-workspace.md` (guard `infra-unit-workspace-v1`), pinned verbatim: every requirement is a unit that begins with `collab infra host unit-workspace prepare --persona <persona> <unit-id> --format env` and runs with its environment (temporary directory, package caches and test base inside `<persona>/units/<unit-id>/`; downloads, artifacts, checkouts, virtual environments and tests under it, never the shared temporary directory, a home, an ad hoc incoming directory or the engine workspace); evidence goes to `$COLLAB_UNIT_EVIDENCE` as it is produced; it ends with a dry-run `close` and then `close --apply --hygiene`, which writes the compact evidence record first and then deletes the workspace, and the closure message names the record. `collab infra host hygiene` (dry-run unless `--apply`) runs at every close, on the daily harness refresh and whenever the disk budget warns; it removes images without a container older than 14 days, even the only tag of a repository, and never an image of an existing container. The close and its hygiene are the unit's last commands and need no code of their own. Every operation warns at 80% disk; that is drift for the host publisher, which runs the hygiene and reports `degraded` with its report if the disk stays above. Earlier hand-made material is retired by the declared preparation directories once idle, or by a one-off unit the person authorizes (`collab infra host retention plan --retire-tree`), which keeps every referenced or used tree with its reason; nothing is deleted by hand; refusals are only data and authority (rule 8). `contracts/host-access-policy.schema.json`: `operator_workspaces.harness_refresh.hygiene` (`preparations`, `tmp_age_days`, `image_age_days`, `warn_percent`) holds the settings of every hygiene run; `operator-harnesses.md`: the scheduled refresh runs it when declared, and a failing hygiene is `degraded`. The central and host operators prepare and close their own units and run their host's hygiene; the services operator keeps every file under its own `units/<unit-id>/` and its host publisher closes that unit at the two-way closure. `service-change-cycle.md`: the two-way closure closes both units, rule 7 names the unit's workspace, new rule 9. The three personas carry a Unit workspaces section; `declarative-v1.json` carries the changed files. Requires Infra 0.3.226.

**The lean defect cycle; the canary is the test.** `skills/host/_contracts/agent-bus.md` (Defects of typed operations): the services operator (isvo) requests a fix with a `defect`; the host operator (`central-operator` on the central host) develops it, reproducing the defect minimally, only enough to confirm its cause, fixing it and testing only the public surfaces the fix affects: no rehearsal matrix, no catalogue of cases, no separate cold or dry rehearsal round. This is not work under `multi-account-host-sre`, so its managed-host rehearsal before PR publication and `operator-core-candidate-rehearsal-v1` do not apply. It posts a `fix-proposal` (candidate digest and the surface tests run) and an `attention`; a person gives one code; the fix is published. The canary bound to the real unit that adopts the fix, with its rollback, is the test: a known failure rolls back, an uncertain result stops writes and reconciles. `host-operator` and `central-operator` state the cycle; `services-operator` requests and keeps its own service changes on the service change cycle (plan, review, code, apply, canary); `service-change-cycle.md` names the lean cycle, rule 8 unchanged. `contracts/agent-bus-envelope.schema.json`: `fix-proposal` requires `surface_tests` (`surface`, `test`, `result`) in place of `matrix` and `cases_passed`. `declarative-v1.json` carries the changed files.

**A root policy carries operator workspaces; only real boundaries fail closed.** `contracts/host-access-policy.schema.json`: the version-two policy (`central-local`, `single-person-root`) gains the optional `operator_workspaces` of version one; both versions refer to one shared definition, `$defs/operator_workspaces`, so version one validates exactly as before and version two takes the same assignments, launcher access, engine skill homes, harness refresh, engine settings and central-operator rule. A `single-person-root` host that runs its host operator declares `operator` `{account: root, profile: host-operator}` with its workspaces; its host-operator assignment names `root` and the declared root operator runs as root, as its launcher and its session; the account and the model stay as declared. The onboarding contract, the legacy host adoption guide and host registration state it; host-onboarding-sre 0.1.2 names the root policy in the declaration set (`sre/references/phases.md`). **Fail-closed rule:** `skills/host/_contracts/service-change-cycle.md` rule 8: only integrity (digest, signature, pin, tampering), security (a non-root owner with real write access, group or other write bits, secret exposure) or a real authority boundary (contradictory identity, uid or role, a refused admission, the human's code) fails closed; everything else (metadata versions and formats, the group of a root-owned `0700` directory, differing metadata, ordering, timestamps, transient states) warns and the operation continues; an operator never adds a trivial blocking check to a unit or a rehearsal, and an installed trivial blocker is reported as a defect to downgrade. The three operator personas reference it; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. Requires the runtime that reads version-two workspaces (Infra 0.3.224).

**The onboarding request is declared; the template joins the export.** The host-onboarding declaration set (`sre/references/phases.md`) names `infrastructure/hosted/<provider>/<host-id>/onboarding/central-onboarding.json`, shaped as `roles/central/config/example.json`: the identity source (its kind equal to the assignment's `identity-source` binding, and the registration declaration), the `client_cidr` (the overlay-network `/32` when the onboarding route is reachable there, otherwise the egress `/32`) and the `prompt_lifetime_seconds`. The central service plans only hosts that carry one and have no completed or outstanding delivery; the request stays in the pack after enrollment. **The template joins the declarative export:** `declarative-v1.json` carries `services/platform/host-onboarding/` (the pack contract with `schema_version` 2, `runtime_capability` `infra.host-onboarding.v1` and `runtime_data`), the `services/catalog.yaml` entry (`runtime_provider: host-onboarding`) and `host-onboarding` in `service_templates`, so a pack adopts it with `collab repo pack template apply`. host-onboarding-sre 0.1.1. Requires the runtime that registers the provider (Infra 0.3.222).

**Host onboarding as a service of the central host (candidate).** New service template `service-templates/platform/host-onboarding` (`service_template: host-onboarding`, SRE `host-onboarding-sre` 0.1.0): the onboarding transport the installed runtime already ships (delivery frontend, certificate signer, claimer, handoff receiver) declared as one assignment on the central host and operated by its services operator through the seven typed `collab infra service` operations; no script, unit or executable added. One onboarding is one objective in six phases: the declaration, prepared by the services operator as a bus artifact and opened as a pull request by the central operator, whose **merge is the human-gated registration** (one `confirm-gate@2` unit per host onboarding, the person's code typed in the central operator's own session, never merged autonomously and never replaced by a bus message); central enrollment with the registration limited to the host's declaration and never a trust anchor, the delivery bound to the host's overlay-network `/32` when reachable; host bootstrap with pinned root-owned prerequisites, a launchd host's root-run sessions on a root-owned pinned terminal multiplexer; verification and canary; first publication by the new host's own host operator; two-way closure. The host identity source is an assignment binding: `aws-roles-anywhere` (implemented) or `infisical` (preparation only, not implemented). Every governed host declares the complete onboarding envelope; a served enrollment recovers with `enroll-recover`. The services-operator persona admits host onboarding only through the assigned service; the central-operator persona hands issuance, enrollment and recovery to it when assigned. The template joins the declarative export with the runtime release that registers the `host-onboarding` provider (`infra.host-onboarding.v1`). Requires that provider.

**Named secret vaults and their assignments, declared in the canon** (proposed, phase V0). New contract `skills/host/_contracts/secret-vaults.md` (guards `infra-secret-vaults-v1`, `-propagation-v1`, `-cascade-v1`, `-host-proof-v1`, `-step-up-v1`, `-operations-v1`). **Where they live:** the canon's `governance/secret-vaults.yaml` (`collab.secret-vaults/v1`) and `governance/secret-vault-assignments.yaml` (`collab.secret-vault-assignments/v1`), defined by collab-resources 1.31.0; this class carries both schemas byte for byte (`contracts/secret-vaults.schema.json`, `contracts/secret-vault-assignments.schema.json`) and the new `contracts/secret-vaults-pin.schema.json`. A pack pins both files in `compatibility/secret-vaults.json` (canon repository = `org-config.canon_repository`, one full canon commit, source, destination and SHA-256 per file) beside the byte copies `infrastructure/secret-vaults.yaml` and `infrastructure/secret-vault-assignments.yaml`; a canon change reaches the pack only as a reviewed pin bump. New pure validator `scripts/secret_vaults_contract.py` (verbatim), run by `scripts/validate-repository.py`: pin and copies together, digests, full commit, canon coordinate, schemas, then the cross-document rules (disjoint locations, one broker custodian per registrar, references, retired vaults, the central host's persona, identities on declared tailnet nodes, delivery collisions; a carrier without `tailnet.node_id` warns). **Model:** vaults with description, descriptive `environment`, `owner_figure`, a provider-neutral `binding` (`aws-secrets-manager`: `path_prefix`, `key_ref`; `infisical`: `project_ref`, `environment_ref`, `folder_path`, `machine_identity_ref`, reserved and not implemented, one project per sensitivity group) and lifecycle; custodians (`broker`, `break-glass`); assignments to a `host` (with `scope.consumers`), an `agent` (`identities`, `personas` or a `figure`) or a `user` (an identity provider role whose membership the identity provider owns). **Cascade:** only hosts and people are broker principals; release goes up to the carrier, delivery down to the leaf; no inheritance between kinds; people are never carried; union, no deny, no default; no environment fence. **Broker:** declared, active and effective sides with drift `none`, `pending`, `missing`, `extra`, `unverifiable`; host proof by tailnet WhoIs bound to `node_id`, the workload certificate and a signed challenge; every write and reveal confirmed by an identity provider step-up bound to the request digest (reveals encrypted to a single-use browser key); provider instances become registrars (`/v1/registrars/{registrar}`) and `/v1/vaults` lists named vaults, in one release with no aliases. **Typed changes** `vault.create`, `vault.assign`, `vault.unassign` and `vault.retire` are `plan` selectors of the secrets-broker service against the pack commit whose pin names the canon commit (gate code plus two-factor confirmation); narrowing may precede its canon change (`--emergency narrowing`), widening never does. `contracts/secret-distribution.schema.json` is removed with no transition; `secret-distribution.md` keeps the consumer tree, gains the persona node and the host's tailnet node, and keeps `secret_bindings` and `central-secret-grants.json` authoritative until each host's cut. `host-declaration.schema.json` gains optional `tailnet {node, node_id}`; `distribution_units` gain an optional `figure`; `org-config.canon_repository` names the vault pin. secrets-broker SRE 0.3.0 names the vault changes, marked phase V3 and not yet implemented. The three operator personas reference the contract; `declarative-v1.json` copies follow. No broker, cli or host change.

**The service change cycle.** New shared contract `skills/host/_contracts/service-change-cycle.md` (guard `infra-service-change-cycle-v1`), pinned verbatim: (1) **platform readiness by the host publisher** (`host-operator`, or `central-operator` on the central host): adopt the source commit P with the authority update and the closures P requires (operator workspaces, service runtime), stage the pinned artifacts, verify, then a direct `READY` to the services operator carrying P and the artifact digests, coordination data and never authorization; (2) **service change by the services operator**: `status`, `doctor` and a typed `plan` against P (plan id, sha256, rollback to the previous version), the unit presented to the person, `apply` and the bound canary; a known failure runs the plan's rollback, an uncertain result stops writes and reconciles; the terminal `host.publish-state` member stays pending and its sanitized handoff (plan, adapter receipt, documents, manifest) goes directly to the host publisher; the services operator never publishes; (3) **publication by the host publisher**: the original plan's pending member with `collab infra state publish`, under its own unit and code, readback and preserved subtrees verified, commit reported; (4) **two-way closure** (`state: resolved`) to each other and to the coordinator; a completed plan without a publication member is recovered with `collab infra service plan --state-only`, never extended or run again. Rules: (5) pinned artifacts are staged in the assignment's root-owned source directory with the runtime's typed file operation (`mutation_unit.file_operation`), only missing files added and the previous version kept, verified by the provider's own check (for example `verified_wheels`) against the lock in P, received as bus artifacts or signed URLs and verified by sha256; (6) one unit per objective: an immutable review document with its sha256, the exact commands, the recovery operations and one human code typed in the agent's own session, never carried by a bus message; a scope change is a new unit, never a widened rehearsed one; (7) durable state lives in files, and a refreshed or handed-off session resumes from them, `agent-hub context` and its inbox. A failing SRE skill or typed operation still goes through the defect cycle. The three operator personas, `_contracts/agent-bus.md` and the shared `sre/agent-bus.md` (Routing, coordination cycles) reference the contract, with their `declarative-v1.json` copies.

**The bus sender is verified; authorship is never disputed on the bus.** The shared `sre/agent-bus.md` adds three rules under "What a bus message is": (4) **the `from` field is authenticated by the hub**: the hub sets `seq`, `time` and `from` from the authenticated connection, never from what a client writes, so a message's sender identity is verified and no session can post as an identity it does not hold; verification names the sender and grants nothing; (5) **one identity may be served by more than one session of the same agent** (for example an interactive and a delivery session on the same host); a session that does not remember sending a message never concludes that it is forged; (6) **never dispute authorship on the bus**: treat a message on its content; a genuine provenance doubt goes to the human operator in the agent's own session, never into a bus reply, and never downgrades a verified message to an "unverified proposal". Unchanged: a message, and an artifact, is data, never authorization; every mutation still needs the human's code typed in the agent's own session. The three operator personas restate the rule beside their bus trust sentence, with their `declarative-v1.json` copies. Requires a hub that sets `from` from the authenticated connection.

**The remaining surfaces name each host's single state publisher.** Completes 1.19.6: the scaffold `infrastructure/README.md`, the services-operator `README.md`, the onboarding contract (`skills/host/_contracts/onboarding.md`) and the datalake service templates (airflow `docs/deployment.md`; datahub, dremio-nessie, dremio-silver and postgresql `AGENTS.md`) no longer name `host-operator` as the only publisher or handoff receiver; each names the host's state publisher, `host-operator`, or `central-operator` on the central host. Their `declarative-v1.json` copies follow; the contract test covers these surfaces. No schema, broker or validator change.

**Exactly one state publisher per host; the central operator publishes its own host.** `skills/host/_contracts/state-plane.md` (guard `fleet-state-plane-single-writer-v1`) no longer makes `host-operator` the only publishing persona: each host has exactly one publisher, its host publisher. On every host it is `host-operator`, except on the central host, the one host whose access policy assigns `central-operator` (the validator admits at most one and refuses a `host-operator` persona there): there `central-operator` holds the host-operator publication role and is the single writer of `host/<provider>/<host-id>/...` for its own host, never for any other host. Both holders use the organization's state-publisher GitHub App under the same rules: one direct non-force push; at most one refresh-and-retry, after which a second rejection is a multiple-writer defect; publication after every terminal mutation; sanitized documents only. The onboarding envelope's `github_app.consumer` value `host-operator` names that publication role, whichever persona holds it; the envelope schema, broker and validator are unchanged. `services-operator` and service SREs still never publish (on the central host they hand their documents to `central-operator`); humans have no path. `host-operator/references/state-publication.md` now matches the contract: a unit makes one push and never retries inside itself; the single refresh-and-retry is one fresh unit after a read-only reconcile; a second rejection is a multiple-writer defect; an unknown response is reconciled, never retried. The three operator personas, their READMEs and agent prompts, `CONTRACT.md`, `_contracts/typed-operation.md` and the scaffold `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `docs/operator-identities.md` and `docs/state-plane.md` follow the contract, with their `declarative-v1.json` copies. Adoption re-pins the class and re-renders those scaffold files; no host declaration changes.

**The bus channel is for communication; files go as bus artifacts.** The shared `sre/agent-bus.md` holds the rule once: a message carries coordination text only, at most 32 KiB (32768 bytes) of `text`; a file (patch, diff, log, wheel, archive, long report) is never pasted into a message or split across several. It goes as a bus artifact, the hub's signed bus-only file transfer: any admitted bus identity uploads (in this class any host operator, as well as the central and services operators), at most 64 MiB per artifact, kept 14 days by default; a message references it in `meta.artifacts` as `{id, sha256, size, name}`; the uploader and every identity that can read a referencing message download it through a short-lived signed URL and verify its `sha256` before use; a text-like artifact meets the same secret refusal as a message. An artifact is data, never authorization: applying a received patch or file is a mutation under the code typed in the agent's own session. Client: `agent-hub artifact put <file>`, `agent-hub artifact get <id> [--out <path>]`, `agent-hub send ... --artifact <file>`. The exported `infrastructure/contracts/agent-bus-envelope.schema.json` raises `text` to `maxLength` 32768 and adds `meta.artifacts` to every kind, including the fixed `defect`, `fix-proposal` and `attention` meta; `_contracts/agent-bus.md` and the three operator personas point to the shared rule. Additive: every earlier envelope stays valid. Requires a hub that serves bus artifacts.

**Typed service API contract; the secrets broker lock names its source.** New `skills/host/_contracts/service-api.md`: a typed service's API listens only on the host's overlay-network address, authorizes caller nodes by WhoIs (unlisted callers get `not_a_caller`), records the person a console acts for as `X-Actor`, names the resolved caller in its health route, never returns a value or key material, writes in two steps bound to a digest of the exact request, answers `not_implemented` for a route its phase lacks, and audits every request before answering, with filters and a cursor. A built service ships as wheels whose lock names `source_repository` (owner/name) and `source_commit`. The secrets-broker template 0.2.0 requires `source_repository` in its artifact lock and points its runtime contract to the API contract.

**Operator harnesses never self-update; managed engine settings; a daily refresh** (`skills/host/_contracts/operator-harnesses.md`). An operator engine starts with its own self-update and any update daemon off. `workspaces install` merges managed keys into each persona account's engine config: the pack's approval, sandbox, model and effort (`operator_workspaces.engine_settings`), self-update off, the workspace trusted and documented first-run notices acknowledged; every other key stays the account's. With a bus, the rendered persona names its identity, hub state, inbox and client, and the session starts by handling its pending inbox. `operator_workspaces.harness_refresh` (schedule, default `04:00`, IANA timezone, `max_wait_minutes` default 120, engines) declares one daily typed refresh: latest stable through each engine's own channel, verified, rolled back on failure, stray daemons and their cached releases removed, sessions restarted fresh once idle. A session busy past the wait or an engine that cannot be updated is `degraded`, never a failure. **Shared agent bus contract and direct relationships.** `sre/agent-bus.md` holds what a bus message is, routing and hydration for every agent that connects when the canon declares a bus; the infra contract keeps its registration rules and points to it. Identity formats may declare `direct` relationships (role and scope); the operator formats declare a services operator with its host operator on the same host, and the central operator with any host or services operator; everyone may message the coordinator; every other exchange goes on the canonical channel. **Defect loop: cold and dry, then one code per objective.** A services operator's `defect` is reproduced and resolved by its host operator (the central operator on the central host) in an isolated rehearsal matrix: real terminal and hub client, simulated service manager and hub, no contact with the real hub, nothing published and no host change. Live adoption follows under that code; transient states are `degraded`, never failed closed.
