**Only evidence files become durables, after the secret filter; retention never removes them.** Public is limited to durable candidates: `captures/*.png`, `hierarchy/*.json` and `journey/*.json` whose `schema` is `journey-captures-v1` or `journey-hierarchy-v1`; reports, arbitrary HTML, traces, videos and logs stay private. Each candidate is searched, before upload, for the run's secret values held in memory (any length, raw or JSON-escaped, and in the decoded JSON strings) and for credential shapes; one that holds either is published private, named under `withheld` in the manifest and the receipt and warned in the job log, as are the non-durable objects a public request leaves private. A text object that names a forbidden host keeps its visibility and is warned in the job log instead of failing the publication (a hostname is not a secret). On `/mobile` the vault detection follows `runFlow` and `runScript` includes, an unreadable include counts as a read, and from the first such flow every capture and hierarchy of the job stays private. `secrets[]` follows the common contract `{name, kind, source}` (`kind` `hydration-token` or `vault`, `source` `vault:<surface>/<repository>/<entry>`), never a value; a declared secret with no usable value in memory (empty, partial, or after a restart) and a `/mobile` replay that did not finish (cancelled, timed out, failed) make the publication private with a warning. Retention removes only private objects: the durables and their manifest (`evidence.durable_keys`) never expire. HTML, JS, CSS, CSV and SVG objects are redacted too. [`references/evidence.md`](references/evidence.md) keeps only the service configuration and links the [artifact publication](../../skills/artifact-publication/SKILL.md) rule.

**A hydrated run may publish public durables** (owner decision D8 of the single artifact-publication plan, 2026-11-16). The rule that forced `private` on every run with hydrated variables is retired: on `/web`, `captures/`, `hierarchy/` and `journey/` follow `evidence.visibility`; logs, results and traces stay private. On `/mobile` only a flow that reads a vault entry keeps its capture and hierarchy private. Hydrated values are not secrets and are no longer redacted; the hydration token and the vault entries are, and the receipt's new `secrets[]` names them (`hydration-token`, `vault-entry`), never their values ([evidence](references/evidence.md#visibility), [hydration](references/hydration.md#receipt)).

**Hydration probe tools on both surfaces.** `hydration_take`, `hydration_release`, `hydration_check` and the raw pass-through `hydration_raw` let an agent that holds no hydrate-token use the hydration endpoint of a repository the instance serves: the service sends the request with the repository's delivered token (the request code of a run, now shared) and returns the hydrated values to the caller, by the owner's rule; the token appears in no output, log, record, error message or exception text. `take` returns `{status, variables, fixture_id, expires_at}`, `release` deletes a fixture from its own record (token, repository and base are never the caller's), `check` returns the key names only and releases at once, and `raw` forwards a GET, POST or DELETE under `/v1/environment/hydrate/` and returns the whole answer, errors included (the repository whose token is used is explicit; a caller Authorization header is dropped; the token is scrubbed from every header and body). A base outside staging/qa is refused at the call as at load. Each take, release and raw call leaves a names-only record (`hydration_probes`, `hydration_raw`), and each failed or refused attempt a row in `hydration_failures`; an answer that echoes the token in its fixture id, expiry or a variables key is refused and recorded nowhere, and a fixture created with unusable variables is deleted before the error. A DELETE is never sent to an address that is not one fixture (an id that is empty, `.` or `..`) or that holds the token: such a fixture is reported unreleased and expires. A body is scrubbed of the token and of the forms an endpoint writes an echoed bearer in (JSON escapes, `\/`, HTML entities, percent-encoding). A body cut at the cap loses a fixed margin at its end, so what is dropped never depends on the token (a caller whose own text is reflected cannot learn it), and the text never exceeds the cap in bytes. Metadata and shape deviations (another method name, a trailing slash or other segment characters, query characters, a request body over 1 MiB, a scenario spelling, a non-UPPER_SNAKE key, a non-text value) warn and continue; only what leaves the path refuses. Unreleased fixtures expire at `expires_at` ([hydration](references/hydration.md#probe-tools)).

`command-registry.json` pins the released cli's public grammar (`collab.command-registry/v1`, from uxmaltech-collab/cli `docs/command-registry.json`, source in `command-registry.source.json`), and `tests/test_named_commands_exist.py` refuses any `collab ...` route a persona, contract or reference names that the grammar does not register; a sentence that says a route does not exist is not a use of it.

A profile file may declare `syntax: json`: the engine reads the `values` object of one JSON document, with no `pack-profile` markers (the shape of a typed host profile), and reports a document without one as a `profile-keys` finding. Existing python and sh profiles and manifests are unchanged. Engine version 0.7.0.

`host-environment-documented`, `persona-guards` and `adapter-actions-documented` default to warning: documentation and guard-text drift is reported with its owner and `check` exits 0 on it, so a consumer pin test or repository validation continues. A manifest `severity: error` or `--severity warning` still stops; `pin-digests`, `contract-secret-process-variables` and the other rules keep their severity. Engine version 0.6.0.

`shared-doctrine.md` holds the three doctrine paragraphs every SRE `ALIGNMENT.md` embeds between `shared: alignment-doctrine` markers; `tests/test_shared_doctrine.py` keeps the copies equal. Engine behavior is unchanged.
Manifest schema version 1 accepts an optional `intents` block (intent parity) that requires only an `id` per item; `check` ignores it and continues. Existing manifests are unchanged.
Keep the verbatim-doctrine regression tied to the capability-first text instead of the retired release-order sentence. Alignment behavior is unchanged.
Enforce one shared gate bundle with immutable source digests and reject persona copies or aliases.
Artifact-aware work classification, shared lifecycle and immutable consumer adoption.

**Manual recovery exception** (guard `breaking-glass-manual-restore-exception-v1`, owner decision 2026-11-10): restoring access or the typed loop by hand only with the owner present, inside an incident declared to the coordinator, one unit at a time with backup and validation, each step recorded as a cli-owned GAP. The persona uses the host-installed role only inside that incident and is never a permanent operator. Drift doctrine from the shared block. `ALIGNMENT.md` states what is checked; tests use the public `sre-align check` (coherence audit sot-sres F5, F19, F29, F30, F31). Review fix: the restore route the GAP proposes is stated as missing in the same clause that names it.

**Two lanes (OD-053).** New section (guard `two-lane-model-v1`): the owner's two-lane model, and this session is on neither lane; working through it during a round, you never cut a candidate, merge a batch of undeveloped issues or move a pack to an unpublished release, and a code fix goes to the developer for the next composition.
**The conduct doctrine.** `skills/agent-hygiene` is renamed `skills/agent-conduct` (guard `agent-conduct-v1`); the reference follows it, with its new Delegation section.
**Names the role it acts as.** `acts_as` is checked against the registry's `roles`.

**A declared runtime floor.** `version.json` states `requires_runtime` 0.3.554 and `requires_hub_client` 2, computed by `scripts/persona_floors.py` from the commands this persona and its shared doctrine name.
**Hygiene.** A section references the shared `skills/agent-hygiene` (guard `agent-hygiene-v1`) for its own scratch and every host's residue.

**A row taken in an incident runs as written.** Break-glass on the bus (guard `breaking-glass-not-a-coordinator-v1`): a row it takes inside its incident runs as written and closes in merge plan rule 29's closing format; Never: it never redesigns that row (`dispatched-plan-runs-as-written-v1` of `sre/agent-bus.md`), and only an unsupported typed operation or a state without rollback changes a step (infra-resources 1.56.0).

**Not a coordinator.** Break-glass on the bus (guard `breaking-glass-not-a-coordinator-v1`, replacing `breaking-glass-coordinator-roles-v1`): the organization's one coordinator is the canon's `bus.coordinator` (`sre/coordinator`), which plans and dispatches every rollout and adoption; development belongs to the developer (`sre/collab-developer`); this session acts on a host only inside an incident it declares to the coordinator, which pauses the requests queued there, and may take a row there with the owner; the operating loop hands a release to the developer and a rollout or adoption to the coordinator (infra-resources 1.55.0).

**For break-glass only.** The persona keeps emergency access and recovery with the owner behind it: identity, inventory, access routes, acting, mutation authorization, drift doctrine, GAP reporting. Every development, release and rollout responsibility moves to `sre/collab-developer` with its references, `scripts/release`, `scripts/rollout`, their schemas and tests (Affected-host promotion, Complete rollout, Runner canary, Runtime rollout, Release creation and adoption, Rollout preparation, Hosts the rollout reaches, Developer delivery ownership, Developer Collab on runner jobs, Native executor, End-to-end Collab). "Break-glass on the bus" (infra-resources 1.54.0, rules 29 and 30): as `bus.coordinator` it coordinates only the requests it starts, is never dispatched a platform row, and prevails only on the hosts of an incident it declares, where it may take a row.

**Each coordinator coordinates the requests that reach it.** The Coordinator and break-glass section (infra-resources 1.53.0, merge authorization rule 29): this session is the owner's break-glass SRE, leads the whole infrastructure and is alive only while the owner is behind it, never autonomous, unattended or in a loop; it coordinates the requests it started, the canon's `autonomous_coordinator` the rest, and its decision prevails when both act; when its work asks for priority over a request queued with or by the autonomous coordinator, that request is paused or reordered and this session's goes first. The frontmatter version follows `version.json`.

**The coordinator role follows the owner's presence.** The Coordinator and break-glass section (infra-resources 1.50.0, merge authorization rule 29): this session holds the coordinator's role only while the owner is connected in it; at every other time the canon's `autonomous_coordinator` decides, and a decision of this session on the same request prevails. Also carries the agent hub break-glass identity format and the coordinator and break-glass section released since 0.3.31; the frontmatter version follows `version.json`.

**An agents-host round reloads every superseded session before its canary.** The agents procedure that `rollout prepare` names, and `references/runtime-rollout.md`, make it a step of the round: after the adopt, `session-reload` for each session whose image is superseded, Stopped, Idle and Running alike; the host refuses one with a turn in progress untouched, and it is reloaded once idle. A session runs its own image's runtime against the pack the host now serves, so a session left on the previous image can refuse that pack (agents-02, 2026-10-27). A pack change only the new runtime accepts waits until no session runs the previous image.

**Each served tree is scanned by the target runtime before the merge.** `rollout prepare --runtime-python <target runtime>` exports, once per pack a published host serves, every served tree (each generation's `data/`, else the root) and scans it with `collab.declarative.scan_pack`, the way a pack load scans it. Each violation is a `declaration` row with status `violation` that reaches: the load would stop every host that adopts the pack at `authority`, the session broker and the jobs. On 2026-10-27 an evidence-check copy the runtime did not know stopped agents-02 after its served checkouts had moved; the scan names it before the merge.

**A developer runtime over a host's images is a row, and a rollout freezes its inputs.** A developer Collab runtime a host's inventory publishes (`developer Collab runtime declared: ...`, Infra 0.3.183) is an `override` row that reaches: the jobs of its profiles run it instead of the adopted composition, so the rollout does not close while it exists, unless the owner's `--limit`. `rollout prepare --freeze <file>` records at the start the `main` commits of the template clone, runtime, infrastructure, packs and libraries, the agent base and the open pull requests (`collab.rollout-freeze/v1`); `--frozen <file>` at the close moves the rows that exist only because something entered afterwards to `next_rollout`, listed and outside the verdict, so a later merge never blocks this rollout.

**A repository agent the runtime refuses to load is a row.** `rollout prepare --runtime-python <installed runtime>` exports each pack's `main` (the whole tree, as the hosts serve it, at a resolved path) and loads every `repo-agent` of each served generation's catalog (else the root) the way the runner jobs and the image preparation do (`runtime_spec`, `select_capabilities`, for `resolve` and `create-journey`). A refusal is a `declaration` row that reaches: the agent stops before it runs until its declaration loads. Without `--runtime-python` nothing is loaded and the verdict names it as a caveat, so a preparation never reads as clean on what it did not check. Found when two agents declared `skill: summary` without a summary path and every resolve of theirs stopped at "Run the agent" while three closing preparations listed nothing.

**A runner-skill pointer behind its library, or at a commit no catalog links, is a row.** `rollout prepare` reads every `.collab/runner/skills/<skill>.yaml` of every clone it knows (packs, `--consumer`, workspaces); a `source: <owner>/<repo>@<commit>:<path>` is compared with the library clone's `main` like a pack link (`consumer-library` rows, `behind`, with the merges between) and with the pack catalogs: a commit no catalog links is `unlinked`, because the hosts materialize the catalog's commits and the agent reads the pointer's, so the two move together in the repository's own pull request, merged as part of the adopt. The pack links and the pointers share one catalog index, one library distance and one GAP line per library without a clone. Found with two governed repositories pointing executor skills at commits no catalog linked, five releases behind.

**A library a pack skill links is a row when its main moved on.** `rollout prepare` reads every `skills/catalog.yaml` of each pack, root and served generations alike, and compares each `library_links` entry of the form `<owner>/<repo>@<commit>:<path>` with the library clone found among `--library <clone>`, the workspaces or the template clone by its `origin`: the version the linked path states at the pinned commit (`version.json`, `SKILL.md` front matter or CHANGELOG) against the version at the library's `main`, with the merges between; a path that states no version is compared by content. A newer version is a `library` row that reaches: the pack's pull request moves the link in the catalog, the skill's `implementation.yaml` and sidecar manifest in every tree, with the skill's version, CHANGELOG and external-dependency reference, and the hosts that serve the pack materialize it in their round. A library with no clone is an `unknown` row and a GAP line. Found with the design and executor skills of two library repositories three to four releases ahead of the links of five repository-pack skills while every preparation closed at zero rows.

**An adoption plan covers every pin the pack carries.** `release adopt plan` plans a pack that pins several repository classes instead of stopping: `--class` chooses, else the one class that declares an adoption tool at its target release, else the first pinned, and a warning names the others. Every other templates pin the consumer carries outside its test fixtures, the pin of a served generation (`transitions/<generation>/data/compatibility/templates.yaml`), is planned beside the root pin as `pin-diff` rows of its own under `Generation`, with the generation's projection declaration named and the plan hash covering them; `adopt apply` leaves them to the pack's generation route and says so. Found on a repository pack whose served generation pinned a skill one release behind while the plan refused the pack for pinning two classes; the pin moved by hand in the pack's own pull request. The class tool's refusal of a pinned file with local changes stays as it is: it protects a consumer's edits before any write, and its evolution is a merge of the class, not a warning.

**The rollout covers the whole chain, and so does the adopt.** `rollout prepare` counts the `pin` rows (a pack behind a release of the source of truth) and the `consumer-collab`, `governed-files` and `repository` rows (a governed repository behind the agent base the pack serves, lacking a governed file, or unread) among the rows that reach the agents: a pull request of their own repository delivers each, and the rollout opens it and merges it as part of the adopt, after the hosts. The verdict's `pending` bucket is gone, its summary names how many rows those pull requests deliver, and `no rollout` also means every pack pins what is released and every governed repository follows the agent base; new reference section "The chain the adopt covers" (source of truth, canon and packs, hosts, implementation repositories), and a rollout closes only when a preparation run afterwards lists no row. Owner rule of 2026-10-25, found with 22 governed repositories at an agent base two minors behind the one the pack served while every round reported the hosts adopted.

**Declared differences are not drift.** The `generation` comparison of `rollout prepare` leaves out the paths a transition declares under `preserved` (legacy files kept at the root on purpose, with their own schema) and counts as accepted the pairs the pack's ledger `tests/generation-divergences.json` decided `divergent` or `hold`; the row, the WARN line and the host source line name the accepted count beside the drift. Found on a pack whose every remaining difference was declared and whose row reached all the same.

**A served generation that differs from its root is a row, never `adopted` alone.** `rollout prepare` reads each served pack's own projection declaration at its `main` (`transitions/<generation>/projection.json`, or the skills `compatibility/product-projection.json` selects) and compares root and generation by blob in one `git ls-tree`. A difference is a `generation` row that reaches, with the pack's reconciliation route as its next step, a WARN line and `(generation drifted n of m)` beside the host's served source. Found in a repository pack where 238 of 538 bound files differed: a skill a minor version ahead at the root and a version behind in every session and guest image, while every preparation reported its source `adopted`.

**An end-to-end run stops at its finish line.** `e2e-collab`: once the epic is validated, the operator comments the canon's acceptance command (`/acceptance-verified`) on each story-repo whose work orders are merged, reads back the `lifecycle:implemented` state the canon's delivery processor applies, and stops; `/discovery-complete`, `lifecycle:ready-to-harvest`, the knowledge proposal, OKF publication and harvest pull requests start only when the owner asks for the harvest. The gap log gains the owning-layer column and is kept as the run goes. Documentation only.

**Break-glass never frees a disk by hand.** "Never" forbids removing images, containers, volumes or paths on a host to free disk outside the owning SRE's host hygiene protocol (`github-runners-host-sre` `references/host-hygiene.md`); root access does not widen what may be removed. Documentation only.

**A round covers every host the rollout reaches.** `rollout prepare` compares every served source of every published host with its pack's `main`, finding the clone among `--pack` or in the workspace by its `origin`; a source with no clone is a `source … unknown` row that reaches, and a GAP line, where it used to print "no served source named" and leave the host out. `--round <provider/host_id>...` names the hosts of the next round and the listing answers `Round coverage: complete` or `incomplete: <host>: <why>` with exit code 3; a round starts only after `complete` or an owner `--limit` (guard `breaking-glass-rollout-hosts-v1`). Found when five compositions went to the runners hosts only while an agents host kept serving a pack two merges behind its `main`.

**A workaround is a gap.** `e2e-collab` keeps one recoverable receipt per unit whose terminal state cancels its reminders, and reads the agents' commands, not only their outcomes: a workaround an agent applies to finish a step is logged as a gap even when the step succeeds (enviaflores/collab-resources#334: a tech lead redefined `AI_REPO_RESOURCES_ROOT` 22 times in one session and nobody logged it).

**The agent base a governed repository follows is read from its marker.** `rollout prepare` reads `.collab/agent-base.yaml` (repo-agent-base 0.4.23: `component`, `version`) before the `repo-agent-base <version>` mentions of `.collab` and `AGENTS.md`; an invalid marker warns and the mentions decide.

**A preparation reaches every repository the declarations name.** `scripts/rollout prepare --workspace <dir>` reads the chain instead of a hand-written list: the canon's `governance/agent-sources.yaml` (the packs) and `governance/governed-repositories.md` (the governed repositories and their governed files), the repository pack's `work-checkouts.yaml` (repo-agent targets) and its `skills/repo-agent-base` pin, and each governed clone's `.collab` and `AGENTS.md` (the agent base they name). New rows after the host rows: `repository` (`pack-not-cloned`, `no-clone`, `absent`, the last also a GAP line after one `git ls-remote`), `governed-files` (`missing`) and `consumer-collab` (`behind`, `unmarked`); a repo-agent target the canon does not register is a GAP line and an unregistered clone of the organization is listed. The verdict carries them as `pending`: they reach the agents through a pull request of their own repository, never through a round (guard `breaking-glass-rollout-coverage-v1`). `--json` carries `coverage` and `verdict.pending`.

**A preparation says whether a rollout is needed at all.** `scripts/rollout prepare` ends its "entered since" list with a verdict: `no rollout` when nothing pending reaches what the agents and the jobs run (every published host serves its pack's `main` and the units its services run, no ready pull request changes what they read; a cut that moves only the Infra unit, a pin the pack adopts first, a record and skew are backlog), `rollout` with the rows that reach them and why. After `no rollout` the persona warns and cuts, merges and starts nothing until the owner, having read the warning, says to; a request to prepare a rollout is not that go (guard `breaking-glass-rollout-verdict-v1`). `--json` carries `verdict` with `reaches`, `backlog` and `caveats`; the composition row carries the units that moved.

**A preparation says what entered since the last rollout.** `scripts/rollout prepare` lists, per repository and before the rows, the pull requests merged into `main` after the newest rollout record on the template clone's `main`, or after the composition tag or ISO date `--since` names: squash merges by the `(#n)` at the end of the subject, merge commits by their subject and the title in their body, read with local Git from the first-parent history; commits without a pull request are counted. The template clone is compared from the record's commit, the runtime from the composition tag, packs and consumers from the baseline's date. `--json` carries `since` and `entered`.

**The operator may do the owner's steps, never a link's.** `e2e-collab`: the merge under the owner's rule and decisions the owner delegates may be done on the owner's behalf so the run keeps moving and the next handoffs are exercised; that subsidizes the owner, not a link, and is not a gap. Fixes, review, validation and labels inside the pull request stay with the agents (owner directive, 2026-10-20).

**The e2e-collab operator watches and fixes the agents; it never subsidizes them.** "End-to-end Collab" and `references/e2e-collab.md`: new section "The operator": no dispatch, fix pushed to a pull request, review receipt, delivery or lifecycle label, work-order text or merge in a link's place (the pull-request reviewer applies `pr:ready-validated`); a diverging link is recorded, steered back through its own route, fixed at its source (source of truth, canon or `.collab`) by a merged and adopted pull request, and rerun as the canary of the fix. The operating rules become checks of the links; the gap log records evidence, steering and the correcting pull request; the final report lists the operator actions that did a link's work as gaps (owner directive, 2026-10-20).

**An epic is carried end to end through the Collab agents, and the gaps are the second deliverable.** New section "End-to-end Collab" and `references/e2e-collab.md` (`e2e-collab`): the finish line names the epic's declared environment and the gap list; each link (product manager, tech lead, UX/UI, side-wing repository agent, resolver, pull-request reviewer, merge rule) acts through its own agent and the operator never dispatches, authors or merges in its place; operating rules for autosuggestions, issue bodies as the resolver's whole contract, sizing `--effort=`/`--model=` from the work order, merges only with no resolver run in flight, and review against the live schema; one gap-log row per gap and a final report grouped by owning layer (source of truth, organization canon, repositories' `.collab` resolver and reviewer rules, host configuration) (owner directive, 2026-10-20).

**A rollout is prepared before any unit, and the owner's real jobs are the canary.** New `scripts/rollout prepare` computes the rows of "Complete rollout" from local clones and one pull-request listing per repository (replayable from a file): ready behavioral pull requests of the source of truth, the runtime, the canon, the packs and the governed consumers, with drafts, decision records, dependency bumps and consumer feature work reported outside; the composition still to cut; the rollout record still to write; pack pins behind their latest release row, served generations included, with the releases between; the runtime and served sources of every published host inventory, in delivery order with the next step of each; one round entry per host (Linux runners, macOS Tart, agents) with the owning procedure; and the cut readiness of a wheelhouse (every locked wheel present with its digest) and a build venv, plus the version modules against their project versions. Output schema `collab.rollout-prep/v1`; `references/rollout-prep.md` carries the rows, the rounds, the traps and the evidence of adoption. "Runner canary" (guard `runner-canary-real-jobs-v1`, text only): after a round the owner's own real jobs on the lane are the canary, read on the host; a cosmetic canary issue is opened only when the owner asks (owner directive, 2026-10-19).

**The pull requests still to enter are rows of a rollout; an ADR is not.** "Complete rollout" adds to the distance the open pull requests of the source of truth, the canon and the packs that are ready to merge and change how the agents or the ecosystem behave; an ADR, a draft knowledge record or a dependency bump outside the source of truth is reported as a draft or out of scope and never merged for the rollout. `references/promotion.md` step 5 lists them once per repository and leaves their merge to the repository's review policy, asking before any administrative override.

**A rollout request covers the whole distance.** New normative section "Complete rollout" (guard `breaking-glass-complete-rollout-v1`): a rollout asked from the source of truth and the canon covers every pack component pinned behind its latest release row (root pins and served generations), the runtime of every host against the latest even composition, every served source behind its pack's `main` and any pending release record, presented as the finish line of the first reply. Open pull requests and the named change are inputs, never the boundary; "adopt only task-selected components" and "recreate only what the change affects" decide what one adoption or one round contains, never what the rollout covers; a row the owner excludes stays reported as outstanding coverage. `references/promotion.md` gains the local-Git mechanics per row and the order gate, classes, packs (one pull request each, the canon first), hosts; `references/runtime-rollout.md` states the rule before the round rule.

**Measure before changing a slow rollout.** `references/runtime-rollout.md` names the two timing sources, `publish/apply-timing.jsonl` (Infra 0.3.146) and the Mac executor's `native phase` lines (Runners 0.3.30), with what rollouts v0.3.184 to v0.3.190 measured and changed: one worker publishes consecutive images (Infra 0.3.150), an iOS job hashes its image once per executor (Runners 0.3.32), and an Infra-only release rebuilds no image. No guard changes.

**Hygiene keeps what a Mac round's inputs name.** `references/runtime-rollout.md`: on a macOS Tart host, keep every path the newest round's `round-inputs.json` names (host plan, host pack checkout, projected data, source binding, image inputs), even inside an old round directory. Rollout v0.3.184 lost them and the executor upgrade refused until the round was rebound to the current pack source. No guard changes.

**A rollout lasts as long as its slowest host plus the canary.** `references/runtime-rollout.md` gains "Keeping a rollout short": start every host at once, start in the quiet window, iterate on a dev prefix and release once, the serial image publication as the slow step (rollout v0.3.182: 10 images in 14 of 20 minutes), the native capacity that follows the Mac through `macos_host host-resources` and `native_binding_input --host-resources` (Infra 0.3.142), a capacity proven with as many native canaries, and jobs watched on the hosts. "Hygiene that keeps what is still used" lists what names a prefix or checkout before it is removed. No guard changes.

**The canary and the round follow the affected surface.** The runner canary asked for one job per lane after any change; a lane is now affected only when the round built its image, recreated its controller or changed a unit its job runs. `references/runtime-rollout.md` gains the rule that a host adopts a round only when `collab infra rollout plan` shows something to recreate, and that a pack lock pull request is never a precondition for a host.

Two rollout rules in `references/runtime-rollout.md`. Keep a served checkout readable: run `git` on a pinned checkout under umask 022, list after each move the files an unprivileged user cannot read, and repair from the Git index. Prove a session command inside a running session container, as its user and with the pack it mounts. A round left pack files with mode `600`; host checks run as root and did not see it, and the first command that read the whole pack as the session user failed in every session. No guard changes.

Rollout rules a failed round showed were missing in `references/runtime-rollout.md`: deliver the gate release, its repository classes and the packs before the hosts; preflight every pack the authority names before the authority moves; pack a release on macOS without AppleDouble files; stop a move at the first failed step; stop a detached round and recover the authority. The agents procedure is named at its real path. `references/release.md`: plan the final head before the merge, and adopt a declarative instance with its specification, its files rendered from the runtime lock, a generation that selects part of a class, and a consumer with a tree and a generation. No guard changes.

`references/runtime-rollout.md` named `authority install` for any round that moves the service source. That is the runners-host route. An agents host keeps its pinned checkout: it is fast-forwarded first and named in the move with `authority update --service-source`, as the owning SRE's procedure states. Instructions only: no guard text or script changes.

New "Release creation and adoption": `scripts/release` plans a release from a repository's `release-couplings.yaml` (`create plan`), binds released components to one runtime composition (`create record`, `collab.rollout/v1`) and plans and applies a consumer adoption through the class's own tool, a pack inspector or a pin comparison (`adopt plan`, `adopt apply`). Schemas `collab.release-couplings/v1` and `collab.rollout/v1`.

`SKILL.md` is the single normative source of its verbatim guards (`alignment.yaml` names `source: SKILL.md`); the README summarizes each guarded section and points to it. `Runtime rollout` and `Developer Collab on runner jobs` move verbatim to `references/`, the native executor notes join `references/native-executor.md`, and a `References` section indexes every reference. No obligation or guard id changes.

A one-person organization declares its break-glass owner without `governance/break-glass.yaml`: when the pack's `compatibility/org-config.yaml` carries `operating_model.mode: one-person`, its `steward` is the one owner and its `infrastructure_repository` the controlled repository. An explicit declaration, when present, decides alone. The pack's declaration file is no longer an unconditional alignment obligation.
Return developer installation findings to their owning SRE, preserve declared optionality and identities and require the corresponding normal delivery and acceptance.
Require developer ports to preserve each executor's authority, concurrency and recovery controls and qualify the supported operating system.
Require developer repairs to reach their owning SRE, reviewed runtime distribution, declared image and normal consumer execution path; retain exact acceptance and delivery limits.

New "Native executor": watch a native job in the executor's job row, cancel a run the executor failed before its runner started, take the first job as the proof of a new guest image, and rerun and diagnose a failed session preparation by hand before rebuilding or releasing. New `references/native-executor.md` with the commands: the job row and its reasons, inspecting a sealed image read-only, a hand-driven guest session, moving a tool of the guest and getting a fix to a host. Rollout rules: read the engine each native guest carries after a harness update, stage a release root-owned, split an adoption into plan and apply, and the way back of a native lane is the controller's previous binding.

Resolve every affected declared host and installed service before promotion, prepare one coverage matrix and authorized round, and account for per-host adoption, canary, recovery and outstanding work.

Access is confirmed by one non-interactive login attempt per reported route, even when the route's key fingerprints are empty or omit the owner's key; the report names the accepted key. Routes may carry `key_fingerprints_read_at` (the host's last root reading).

Owner break-glass persona run from a workstation clone: declaration-gated organizations (`collab.break-glass/v1`), host-reported routes and inventory read from `state` (`collab.host-inventory/v1`), GAP reporting, typed-loop service changes and access-only direct writes.

**Public release index.** `references/release.md` gains step 6: after a release of the source of truth merges, or a `vX.Y.Z` tag of a repository listed in `sources.json` of `uxmaltech-collab/releases` is pushed, the developer regenerates `releases.json` there with `scripts/build_index.py` from the fetched clones and commits it to `main` (version, date and changelog of each release, and a SoT row's commit). The Collab console reads that public index with no credential for its «Desfase» page (owner decision, 2026-11-16: uxmaltech-collab has a public release process the console reads). `AGENTS.md` points to the step. A stale index blocks nothing. Floors unchanged.

**The sources of the harness policy binds live in a broker-owned directory.** The broker binds three files read-only into a session container as policy or persona: claude's managed settings at `/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json`, codex's instructions at `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` and grok's MCP policy at `/etc/grok/requirements.toml`. Their sources were staged under the workspace home, in `~/.agent-session/<harness>/`, a directory the account owns. The account could unlink a staged file or rename another over it before the container bound it; the test at bind time (`is_file()` and not a symlink) raced with that; and a file the account put there stayed account-owned and writable while bound, because the in-place rewrite keeps ownership. The read-only flag protects the mount point in the container, not the source. The sources are now staged at `<state root>/session-policy/<workspace id>/<file>`: every directory on that path is root-owned and closed to the account (`_session_policy_file`), so the bind needs no test of the file. One table names the three files (`HARNESS_POLICY_FILES`), and the three binds are read-only, the codex one included. claude's file is still replaced at every start and attach; codex's and grok's are still rewritten in place, so a running container follows them. The directory of a workspace goes with the last session of that workspace, under the broker lock, and the next start creates it again (`_release_session_policy`). An attach releases the lock between reading its row and staging, so it runs the same release after it stages, whether it went on or failed: a stop that closed the session in between leaves no directory behind. A ledger that cannot be read cannot say which workspaces are in use, so the release then removes nothing and does not fail the stop. A container created before this binds the old source: its policy mount reads as missing, so a running one is served as it is until it stops and a stopped one is recreated at its next attach (`_harness_policy_mounts`, now for the three harnesses). The broker no longer writes the old files under `~/.agent-session` and does not delete them; nothing binds them. claude's `mcp.json`, the persona bundle, its provenance and the hooks stay under the home, which the harness reads directly. Adapter 2.31.0 (adapter bytes change; a consumer re-materializes it). **grok keeps its own settings file.** The broker delivered a grok session's MCP servers by binding a generated file over `~/.grok/config.toml`. grok rewrites that file by replacing it, and a bound file refuses the replacement, so nothing a person set or answered there was kept: the model and interface preferences, and the answer to a terms notice, which grok asked again in every new session. The broker now binds nothing over that file: it is the person's own, inside the grok directory their sessions share, so what grok saves there holds for every later session, on any repository agent. The broker never writes an answer for the person. The session's MCP servers are staged as `~/.agent-session/grok/requirements.toml` and bound read-only at `/etc/grok/requirements.toml`, grok's admin layer, with an allow list (`allowed_mcp_servers`, by `server_url` or `server_command`) of exactly those servers. A session without servers gets the policy too, with an empty allow list that blocks every server another file defines, and it replaces the policy an earlier server set left staged. A container created before this keeps the older bind: like a missing cache mount, a running one is served and a stopped one is recreated at its next attach (`_harness_policy_mounts`). claude and codex are unchanged. Checked with grok 1.0.50: the servers of the admin layer are enabled, a same-named block of the person or of a project is ignored, and an added one is blocked. **Support schemas may be scoped to the session.** Two sessions of one account received the same schemas from a support sidecar, so a battery that wipes and migrates them in one session removed the tables of the other. `account_principals` accepts two optional keys. `scope`: `account` (the default, unchanged) or `session`. Under `session` the principal and its secret stay the account's, and each session receives its own schemas `<principal>_<session id>_<suffix>` from its own root-owned file `<account>.<session id>.env`; the account file keeps the secret and is not rewritten when it already holds it. The session stop drops the schemas and removes the file, for the stopped row and for every stale row the broker prunes, and a session that failed to start releases them too. The release runs under the broker lock and drops exactly the schemas the session file records. A stop that arrives while the session is still starting ends that start, which removes the container and the schemas it created. The file reserves the session id: an id is minted again only when no sidecar holds a file for it, and a session start first releases what an earlier stop left. Every release first asks docker whether the session's container is gone; one it cannot confirm keeps its schemas, its file and its id, and a file keeps its id reserved even when the pack no longer declares that sidecar's principals. A release that runs after its id was minted again leaves the new session alone, and a session file that cannot be read keeps its schemas and its reservation. The drop is best effort: a sidecar that is down is reported and never blocks the stop, the file stays and the id stays reserved. Change class: prose, plus code: the client follows no HTTP redirect on any route;
`collab operator-bus close` closes the bus question of a decision answered in the
agent's session; an invalid `--recommended` or `--free-option` warns and is dropped;
the prose adds those rules.

- The client never follows an HTTP redirect, on any route (sre-repos F2): the request and the client token
  never reach the new address. `send` and `close` report `reason: redirected` with the `status` and a
  `location` without credentials, query or fragment; a redirected status query (the settlement of `send`,
  and `outcome`) leaves the outcome unknown, with a warning; `GET /health` follows none either.
- `collab operator-bus close` closes the bus question of a decision that the operator answered in the
  agent's session (sre-repos F6): `POST /v1/answers/close` with `--context decision_id=<id>`, the decision
  id as `send` carries it, or `--answer-id <id>`. It has the protections of `send`: no token in clear text,
  no redirect followed, no body over the bot's 256 KiB. Like `outcome`, it needs no operator setting: its
  request carries none. `describe` lists the operations, read from the registered verbs.
- An invalid `--recommended` (not the position of one `--option`, or not a number) warns and is dropped,
  and the event is still sent (sre-repos F7; EDR-002, fail open); it was a usage error. A wrong
  `--option-code` position still sends nothing, as in 0.1.1. An invalid `--free-option` (not the position of
  one `--option` without a code, or not a number) warns and is dropped, and the event is still sent: a text
  form is presentation, not an effect.
- The prose adds the redirect, `close` and `--recommended` rules to the 0.1.1 rules for option codes,
  buttons, answers and resends.
- Prose guards (`tests/prose_guard.py`, `tests/test_prose_coherence.py`) check that the prose and the
  README name only declared commands and options, and that the package and its documentation carry no
  installation coordinate (sre-repos F13, F14). The README shows tests by path.

- A request with answer buttons is never sent again, even with `retry_safe: true`: the bus keeps its first
  question open in the person's pending list (uxmaltech-collab/cli#1838). A `reconcile_pending` outcome is
  asked again at most three times, then reported as unknown. `send` pauses 30 s before its one status query,
  so its worst case stays under an agent's 2-minute tool limit. An uncertain route the bus does not
  reconcile reports `reason: outcome_unknown`, and a request over the bus's 256 KiB body limit is refused
  before it is sent (`error: request_too_large`), never read as unreachable.
- An unknown outcome is settled, never sent again (uxmaltech-collab/cli#1816). `send`
  waits 60 s for an announcement, longer than the bot waits for Slack (20 s per call,
  and a direct message makes two), and every request carries the client's correlation
  id (`meta.id`). After its own timeout or a lost connection, or when the bot answers
  uncertain routes it reconciles, `send` asks once, 30 s later,
  `GET /v1/announcements/<id>` with the same token: `delivered` reports `sent: true`,
  `not_delivered` reports `retry_safe: true`, and `unknown` or a pending reconcile keeps
  the outcome unknown. Nothing new refuses; the token never appears in the output.
  Every error while the request leaves (a connect timeout, an unreachable host, a failed
  TLS handshake) is `unreachable` at once, never `outcome_unknown` and a status query; a
  2xx answer that cannot be read is settled like any unknown outcome; an unsettled
  reconcile, or one the bot did not start, reports `reason: outcome_unknown`.
  `collab operator-bus outcome --id <id>` asks the bot once, with no wait, so an agent
  asks again later about a reconcile still pending instead of sending again; a request
  with answer buttons that is safe to send again goes with the same `decision_id`.
- `send` gains `--option-code N=CODE` and `--free-option N` (`context.option_codes`,
  `context.free_options`), so an option with an effect opens the bot's code form and a free one its
  text form; the prose asks for one decision per message, in the person's language (owner decision
  OD-074, 2026-11-11; bus side uxmaltech-collab/cli#1823). The bot shows those buttons only for
  `authorization_requested` with `context.decision_id` and `context.requested_by` (the asking identity on
  the agent bus): without them `send` warns and sends the message as asked. A malformed `--option-code`
  names which `--option-code` it was, never any of its value. The prose and the client say how the operator's answer reaches
  the agent (`owner_answer`): a text is data, never authorization, and an effect still needs its code.

- The operator bus SRE (EDR-004): an agent messages its own operator through
  the bot control plane. Equipped by the personas whose `reaches_people` is the
  operator bus: infra-coordinator, collab-developer and breaking-glass (the
  owner); product-manager, tech-lead and ux-ui with their modes (the session's
  person); side-wing (the session's person; in its resolver form, the person who
  dispatched the job). Never by infrastructure operators or the host SREs they
  carry.
- `collab operator-bus send|status|describe` (POST /v1/announcements, GET
  /health), configured at runtime by `COLLAB_OPERATOR_BUS_*`; the host declares
  the operator (`COLLAB_OPERATOR_BUS_OPERATOR`, required), and every message goes
  to the logical destination `operator`; the agent never chooses a person or a
  destination; the previous bot control plane variable names
  warn and continue; the client token never travels in clear text to a public
  address.
- The operator is a GitHub handle, and the bot sends only to the channels that
  person's steward record declares (`Operator-Channel`). When the bot answers
  that the operator declares no channel (`operator_channel_undeclared`) or has
  no steward record (`operator_steward_undeclared`), `send` warns with the
  steward named, prints `sent: false` with `reason` and `steward`, and exits 0:
  the agent continues, and nothing goes to another person or channel.
- A steward record that declares only a channel the bot does not route (a
  Telegram channel, while the bot routes only Slack) is answered
  `operator_channel_unrouted`, with the steward and each unrouted `provider`.
  `send` treats it the same way: it warns, naming the steward and the providers,
  prints `sent: false` with `reason`, `steward` and `providers`, and exits 0.
- The wheel carries `assets/*.json`: the build provenance and dependency lock
  the Collab runtime's layer build writes, against which a host verifies the
  layer pin before it installs it.

layer (`0+unknown` with a warning when the metadata is unreadable); `skills install`
takes `--canon-repository`, warns and continues past a failing skill, and warns on
